And thus, agency, enjoyership, and so forth would appear in two ways — as empirically real (<s>vyāvahārika</s>) and as illusory (<s>prātītika</s>). [Reply:] This would not occur, due to the non-discrimination arising from the sense of identity (<s>tādātmyābhimāna</s>). Or because the inner organ, qualified by all its attributes, is superimposed as a whole upon the <s>ātman</s>, there is no duality. Therefore, since the distinction of knower and so forth is explained for the one <s>ātman</s> alone through the difference of limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>), there is no falling into the Buddhist view, nor any contradiction. Other distinctions will be established more clearly later. Therefore, since the <s>ātman</s>, whose nature is pure consciousness, is invariably present in deep sleep (<s>suṣupti</s>), and since the body, senses, and so forth are variable and objects of perception (<s>dṛśya</s>), the identification of self with those various [entities] by those various philosophers is erroneous — and the <s>Upaniṣadic</s> view alone is authoritative. This is established. || 1 ||

body.text: syād etat / ātmano nirdharmakatve pramātrādivyavahārasyādhyāsamūlatve ca "brāhmaṇo yajeta" ityevamādīnāṃ śāstrāṇām aprāmāṇyaprasaṅgaḥ, akartur abhoktuś cātmanaḥ pravṛttyupapatteḥ, vedāpramāṇye ca kuto brahmasiddhir api, tasya tanmātragamyatvāt, śāstrayonitvād iti nyāyāt / tathā ca vedaprāmāṇyārthaṃ pramātrādivyavahārasya satyatvam abhyupeyam ity āśaṅkya, kiṃ tattvajñānāt pūrvam aprāmāṇyam āpadyate ūrdhvaṃ vā / tatrādye yāvad avidyānivṛttivyavasthāyā upapāditatvāt sarveṣāṃ pramāṇānām avidyāvad viṣayatvena taddaśāyāṃ bādhābhāvān niṣpratyūhaṃ prāmāṇyam / dvitīye tv iṣṭāpattir evety āha --
body.translated_text: One might say: If the <s>ātman</s> is attributeless and practical dealings of the knower and so forth are rooted in superimposition (<s>adhyāsa</s>), then there would be the unwanted consequence of the invalidity of scriptures such as 'A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should sacrifice,' since the <s>ātman</s>, being neither agent nor enjoyer, cannot be motivated to act. And if the <s>Vedas</s> are invalid, whence even the establishment of <s>Brahman</s>, since it is knowable only through them, according to the principle 'because [Brahman] has scripture as its source' (<s>śāstrayonitvāt</s>)? And thus the reality of practical dealings of the knower and so forth must be accepted for the sake of Vedic validity. To this objection [he asks]: Does the invalidity arise before the knowledge of reality or after? In the first case, since the system of removal of <s>avidyā</s> has already been established, all means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇas</s>) have objects only as long as <s>avidyā</s> exists, and in that state there is no sublation, hence their validity is unobstructed. In the second case, it is simply a desired result (<s>iṣṭāpatti</s>) — and so he says:

children.text: na varṇā na varṇāśramācāradharmā na me dhāraṇādhyānayogādayo 'pi /
children.translated_text: Neither the <s>varṇas</s> (castes), nor the duties of <s>varṇa</s> (caste) and <s>āśrama</s> (life-stage), nor <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>yoga</s>, and the like are mine.

children.text: anātmāśrayāhaṃmamādhyāsahānāt tadeko 'vaśiṣṭaḥ śivaḥ kevalo 'ham // 2 //
children.translated_text: Through the destruction of the superimposition (<s>adhyāsa</s>) of 'I' and 'mine' which rests on the non-Self (<s>anātman</s>), that One alone remains — I am <s>Śiva</s>, the Absolute. || 2 ||

body.text: ślokārthaḥ / varṇā brāhmaṇakṣatriyavaiśyaśūdrāḥ / āśramāś ca brahmacārigṛhasthavānaprasthabhikṣavaḥ / ācārāḥ śaucasnānādayaḥ / dharmāḥ brahmacaryagurusevādayaḥ / atra dvandvadvayagarbhaṣaṣṭhitatpuruṣeṇa varṇānām ācārāḥ dharmāś ca āśramāṇām apy ācārāḥ dharmāś ca labhyante / dhāraṇā brahmaṇi bāhyaviṣayatyāgena manasas sthairyam / dhyānaṃ paramātmacintanam / yogaś cittavṛttinirodhaḥ / ādiśabdena śravaṇamananādayo gṛhyante / sarveṣāṃ jñānottarakālam asattve hetum āha -- anātmāśrayāhaṃmamādhyāsahānād iti / anātmā ātmavirodhinī avidyā, tadāśrayas tadupādāno yo 'haṃmamakārādyadhyāsas tasya samūlasyāpi tattvajñānena hānāt tatprayuktavarṇāśramādivyavahāro nāstīty arthaḥ // 2 //
body.translated_text: Meaning of the verse: The <s>varṇas</s> (castes) are <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, <s>Vaiśya</s>, and <s>Śūdra</s>. The <s>āśramas</s> (life-stages) are <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student), <s>gṛhastha</s> (householder), <s>vānaprastha</s> (forest dweller), and <s>bhikṣu</s> (renunciant). <s>Ācāras</s> (practices) are purity, bathing, and so forth. <s>Dharmas</s> (duties) are celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), service to the teacher, and so forth. Here, through the compound containing two <s>dvandvas</s> (copulative compounds) and a genitive <s>tatpuruṣa</s>, we obtain: the practices and duties of the <s>varṇas</s>, as well as the practices and duties of the <s>āśramas</s>. <s>Dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) is the steadying of the mind upon <s>Brahman</s> by abandoning external objects. <s>Dhyāna</s> (meditation) is contemplation of the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>). <s>Yoga</s> is the cessation of mental modifications (<s>cittavṛttinirodha</s>). The word 'and so forth' (<s>ādi</s>) includes hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>), reflection (<s>manana</s>), and so on. He states the reason for the non-existence of all these after the attainment of knowledge: 'Through the destruction of the superimposition of I and mine which rests on the non-Self.' The meaning is: <s>Anātman</s> (non-Self) is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) which is opposed to the <s>ātman</s>; resting on that as its material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) is the superimposition of 'I' and 'mine' and so forth; through the destruction, root and all, of that by the knowledge of reality — the practical dealings of <s>varṇa</s>, <s>āśrama</s>, and so forth do not exist. || 2 ||

body.text: varṇāśramādivyavahārasya mithyājñānamāatramūlatvena mithyātvaṃ draḍhayituṃ tadvyatireke suṣuptau, vyatirekam āha --
body.translated_text: To strengthen the falsity (<s>mithyātva</s>) of the practical dealings of <s>varṇa</s>, <s>āśrama</s>, and so forth as rooted merely in false knowledge — he states their absence in deep sleep (<s>suṣupti</s>) as a negative instance (<s>vyatireka</s>):

children.text: na mātā pitā vā na devā na lokā na devā na yajñā na tīrthaṃ bruvanti /
children.translated_text: Neither mother, nor father, nor gods, nor worlds, nor [Vedic] revelations, nor sacrifices, nor sacred places exist [in deep sleep].

children.text: suṣuptau nirastātiśūnyātmakatvāt tadeko 'vasiṣṭaḥ śivaḥ kevalo 'ham // 3 //
children.translated_text: Since in deep sleep (<s>suṣupti</s>) the nature [of the Self] is devoid of the absolute void — that One alone remains; I am <s>Śiva</s>, the Absolute. || 3 ||

body.text: ślokārthaḥ / mātā janakastrī / pitā janakaḥ pumān / devā indrādayaḥ ārādhyāḥ / lokās tadārādhanaphalāni svargādīni / devāḥ alaukikahitāhitasādhanapratipādakāni brahmapratipādakāni ca pramāṇavākyāni / yajñāḥ svargādisādhanībhūtā jyotiṣṭomādayaḥ / tīrthaṃ yajñasādhanībhūtaḥ kurukṣetrādideśaḥ / evaṃ pāpakarmasādhanāny apy upalakṣaṇīyāni / sarveṣāṃ dehābhimānamūkalatvāt tadabhāve svataḥsambandhābhāvād avidyamānatety arthaḥ / tathā ca suṣuptiṃ prakṛtya śrutiḥ "atra pitāpitā bhavati matāmatā devādevā vedāvedāḥ steno'steno bhavati bhrūṇahābhrūṇahā cāṇḍālo 'cāṇḍālaḥ paulkaso 'paulkasaḥ śramaṇo 'śramaṇas tāpaso 'tāpaso 'nanvāgataṃ puṇyenānanvāgataṃ pāpena tīrṇo hi tadā sarvāñ chokān hṛdayasya bhavati" (BAU 4.3.22) ityādyā abhimānābhāve sarvān arthanivṛttim anuvadanti /
body.translated_text: Meaning of the verse: Mother is the female parent. Father is the male parent. Gods are <s>Indra</s> and others to be worshipped. Worlds are heaven and other fruits of their worship. [Vedic] revelations (<s>devāḥ</s>) are the authoritative sentences that teach both ordinary and extraordinary means of good and evil, as well as those that teach <s>Brahman</s>. Sacrifices are <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and other rites that are means to heaven and the like. Sacred place (<s>tīrtha</s>) is a location such as <s>Kurukṣetra</s> that serves as an instrument of sacrifice. Similarly, the means of sinful action are also implied. The meaning is: since all of these are rooted in identification with the body (<s>dehābhimāna</s>), in the absence of that [identification], they are non-existent due to the inherent absence of any [real] connection. And thus, regarding deep sleep, the <s>Śruti</s> says: 'There a father is not a father, a mother is not a mother, the gods are not gods, the <s>Vedas</s> are not <s>Vedas</s>, a thief is not a thief, an embryo-slayer is not an embryo-slayer, a <s>caṇḍāla</s> is not a <s>caṇḍāla</s>, a <s>paulkasa</s> is not a <s>paulkasa</s>, an ascetic is not an ascetic, a hermit is not a hermit; [the self] is not followed by merit, not followed by sin, for then it has crossed beyond all the sorrows of the heart' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.3.22) — and such [passages] recount the cessation of all things when identification is absent.

body.text: nanu, sarvavyavahārābhāve śūnyataiva syāt / na, ity āha -- nirastātiśūnyātmakatvād iti / nirastam atiśūnyātmakatvaṃ yasmāt tat tathā / bhāvapradhāno nirdeśaḥ / tasya suṣuptisādhakatvāt punarutthānānupapatteś ca / "avināśī vā are 'yam ātmānucchittidharmā" (BAU 4.5.14), "mātrā saṃsargas tv asya bhavati", "yad vaitan na paśyati paśyan vaitan na paśyati" (BAU 4.3.23), "na hi draṣṭur dṛṣṭer viparilopo vidyate, avināśitvāt, na tu taddvitīyam asti tato 'nyad vibhaktaṃ yat paśyet" (BAU) ityādiśrutibhyaś cātmacaitanyasya na suṣuptau śūnyate 'ty arthaḥ / nirākṛtam apy etat punar api sthūṇānikhanananyāyena nirākriyate / yad vā nirastam aśanāyādyatītam advitīyam atiśūnyaṃ yad brahma tadātmakatvāt / tathā ca śrutiḥ "yadā puruṣaḥ svapiti nāma satā somya tadā sampanno bhavati, tad yathā priyayā striyā sampariṣvakto na bāhyaṃ kiñcana veda nāntaram evem evāyaṃ puruṣaḥ prājñenātmanā sampariṣvakto na bāhyaṃ kiñcana veda nāntaram" (ChU VI.9.1) iti / tena jagatkāraṇībhūtasarvajñasarvaśaktiparipūrṇānandabodharūpeṇa brahmaṇā sahaikatvād asaṃsāryeva jīva iti siddham // 3 //
body.translated_text: Objection: In the absence of all empirical activity, the result would be mere voidness (<s>śūnyatā</s>). Answer: No — he says: 'Because it is of a nature in which extreme voidness has been negated.' That from which the nature of extreme voidness has been negated — it is so. The statement is primarily affirmative. Because it [the self] serves as the proof of deep sleep, and because [otherwise] re-awakening would be impossible. From <s>śrutis</s> such as 'This <s>ātman</s> is indeed imperishable, of a nature that cannot be annihilated' (BĀU 4.5.14); 'But there is contact with its elements (<s>mātrā</s>)'; 'That which he does not see there, though seeing he does not see it' (BĀU 4.3.23); 'For there is no cessation of the seeing of the seer, because of its imperishability; but there is nothing second to it, nothing other, separate from it, that it could see' (BĀU) — the meaning is that the consciousness of the <s>ātman</s> is not voided in deep sleep. Though this has already been refuted, it is refuted again by the maxim of repeatedly driving in a post. Alternatively: that which has been negated — [the state] beyond hunger and the rest — is <s>Brahman</s> which is non-dual and supremely void (beyond all); because of having the nature of That. And the <s>śruti</s> [says]: 'When a person sleeps, then, dear one, he has merged with Being (<s>Sat</s>); just as a man embraced by his beloved wife knows nothing outside nor inside, so this person, embraced by the intelligent self (<s>prajñenātmanā</s>), knows nothing outside nor inside' (ChU VI.9.1). Therefore, because of oneness with <s>Brahman</s> — which is the cause of the universe, omniscient, omnipotent, complete bliss, and of the nature of consciousness — the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) is indeed free from <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly bondage). // 3 //

body.text: dvitīyo vibhāgaḥ /
body.translated_text: Second division.

body.text: tatpadārthanirṇayaḥ /
body.translated_text: Determination of the referent of 'tat' (That).

body.text: evaṃ tāvat tribhiḥ ślokaiḥ vādivipratipattinirākaraṇapūrvakaṃ tvampadārtho nirdhāritaḥ / samprati tatpadārthas tathaiva nirdhāraṇīyaḥ / tatra nirākaraṇīyā vādivipratipattayaḥ pradarśyante / nanu, na brahma saha jīvasyaikyam upapadyate / tathā hi sacchabdavācyaṃ jagatkāraṇaṃ brahma "sad eva somya idam agra āsīt" (ChU VI.2.1) ityādivākyena pratipāditam / jagatkāraṇaṃ ca pradhānam acetanam iti sāṅkhyāḥ / paśupatir eva jagatkāraṇam, sa ca cetano 'pi jīvād bhinnaḥ sa upāsya eveti pāśupatāḥ / bhagavān vāsudeva īśvaro jagatkāraṇam, tasmād utpadyate saṅkarṣaṇākhyo jīvaḥ, tasmān manaḥ pradyumnaḥ, tato 'haṅkāro 'niruddhaḥ, tena kāryatvāj jīvasya tena saha na brahmaṇo vāsudevasyātyantābheda iti pañcarātrikāḥ / pariṇāmī nityaḥ sarvajño bhinnābhinna iti jainās tridaṇḍinaś ca / nāsti sarvajñatvādyupetaṃ brahma, āmnāyasya kriyāparatvena tatra tātparyābhāvāt, kin tu vāgdhenvādivat sarvajñatvādiguṇaviśiṣṭatayā jagatkāraṇaṃ paramāṇvādi vā jīvo vā upāsya iti mīmāṃsakāḥ / asti nityajñānādimān īśvaraḥ sarvajñaḥ pṛthivyādikāryaliṅgānumitaḥ, sa ca jīvād bhinna eveti tārkikāḥ / kṣaṇikaḥ sarvajña iti saugatāḥ / kleśakarmavipākāśayair aparāmṛṣṭo nityajñānarūpaḥ pradhānāṃśasattvaguṇapratiphalitatayā sarvajñaḥ saṃsāripuruṣavilakṣaṇa eveti pātañjalāḥ / advitīyaparamānanda eva brahma, tac ca jīvasya vāstavaṃ svarūpaṃ māyayā ca sarvajñatvādiviśiṣṭaṃ jagadupādānaṃ nimittaṃ ceti aupaniṣadāḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus far, by three verses, the referent of 'tvam' (You) has been determined, preceded by the refutation of the contrary positions of disputants. Now the referent of 'tat' (That) is to be determined in the same manner. The contrary positions of disputants to be refuted are here displayed. Objection: The identity of <s>Brahman</s> with the <s>jīva</s> is not tenable. For: <s>Brahman</s>, the cause of the universe denoted by the word 'sat' (Being), has been taught by the sentence 'Being alone, dear one, this was in the beginning' (ChU VI.2.1). The <s>Sāṅkhyas</s> [hold that] the cause of the universe is <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), which is insentient. The <s>Pāśupatas</s> [hold that] <s>Paśupati</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) alone is the cause of the universe; and though He is conscious, He is different from the <s>jīva</s> and is to be worshipped only. The <s>Pāñcarātrikas</s> [hold that] the blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the Lord, is the cause of the universe; from Him arises the <s>jīva</s> called <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, from that the mind called <s>Pradyumna</s>, and from that the ego called <s>Aniruddha</s>; therefore, since the <s>jīva</s> is an effect, there is no absolute identity of it with <s>Brahman</s> (<s>Vāsudeva</s>). The <s>Jainas</s> and the <s>Tridaṇḍins</s> [hold that it is] subject to transformation, eternal, omniscient, and both different and non-different. The <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> [hold that] there is no <s>Brahman</s> endowed with omniscience, etc., since the purport of the <s>Veda</s> lies in ritual action and there is no intended meaning [pointing] there; rather, like the simile of the 'speech-cow,' the thing to be meditated upon is the atoms, etc., or the <s>jīva</s>, qualified by the attributes of omniscience, etc., as the cause of the universe. The <s>Tārkikas</s> (Naiyāyikas) [hold that] there exists an omniscient Lord possessing eternal knowledge, etc., inferred from the effect-signs of earth, etc., and He is indeed different from the <s>jīva</s>. The <s>Saugatas</s> (Buddhists) [hold that] the omniscient one is momentary. The <s>Pātañjalas</s> (Yogins) [hold that] He is of the nature of eternal knowledge, untouched by afflictions, karmic impressions, and their fruits; omniscient through the reflection of the <s>sattva</s>-quality, which is the <s>pradhāna</s>-aspect; and entirely distinct from the transmigrating souls. The <s>Aupaniṣadas</s> (Vedāntins) [hold that] <s>Brahman</s> is non-dual supreme bliss; it is the true essential nature of the <s>jīva</s>; and through <s>māyā</s>, qualified by omniscience, etc., it is both the material and efficient cause of the universe.

body.text: evaṃ vādivipratipattibhiḥ sandigdho tatpadārthe aupaniṣadapakṣasya pariśeṣeṇa tannirṇayāyāha bhagavān --
body.translated_text: Thus, with the referent of 'tat' being in doubt due to the conflicting positions of disputants, the blessed [author] speaks in order to determine it by the method of elimination, [adopting] the <s>Aupaniṣada</s> (Vedāntic) position —

children.text: na sāṅkhyaṃ na śaivaṃ na tat pāñcarātraṃ na nainaṃ na mīmāṃsakāder mataṃ vā /
children.translated_text: [It is] not the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> [view], not the <s>Śaiva</s>, not that of the <s>Pāñcarātra</s>, not the <s>Jaina</s>, not the view of the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> and others.

children.text: viśiṣṭānubhūtyā viśuddhātmakatvāt tad eko 'vaśiṣṭaḥ śivaḥ kevalo 'ham // 4 //
children.translated_text: Because of being of a pure nature [known] through a special experience (<s>viśiṣṭānubhūti</s>), That one alone remains — I am <s>Śiva</s>, the Absolute. // 4 //

body.text: ādiśabdenānuktānāṃ saṅgrahaḥ / na tāvad acetanaṃ jagadupādānam, "tad aikṣata bahu syāṃ prajāyeya" (ChU VI.2.3.) iti īkṣaṇapūrvakasṛṣṭiśravaṇāt, "anena jīvenātmanānupraviśya nāmarūpe vyākaravāṇi" (ChU VI.3.2.) iti jīvātmatvavyapadeśāt, "yasmin vijñāte sarvam idaṃ vijñātaṃ bhavati" (MU I.1.3.) iti caikavijñānena sarvavijñānapratijñānāt, pradhānajñānena ca tadaprakṛtikānāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ jñātum aśakyatvāt, "aitadātmyam idaṃ sarvaṃ tat satyaṃ sa ātmā tat tvam asi" (ChU VI.8.7) iti ca tadabhedasya navakṛtvopadeśāt, "tasmād vā etasmād ātmana ākāśaḥ sambhūtaḥ" (TU II.1.) iti śrutyantarād acetanasya jagatkāraṇatve vicitraracanānupapatteḥ, pradhānamahadāder aprāmāṇikatvāc ca na sāṅkhyamataṃ sādhu / evaṃ pāśupataṃ pāñcarātrikaṃ jainaṃ ca mataṃ śrutiyuktibādhitatvād ayuktam / na ca vidhiśeṣatvāc chrutir na brahma pratipādayatīti mīmāṃsakamataṃ yuktam asiddhatvād vidhiśeṣatvasya / na cārthavādādhikaraṇanyāyād vidhiśeṣatvam, vaiṣamyāt / svataḥprayojanavadarthāpratipādakānāṃ "vāyur vai kṣepiṣṭhā devatā" (TS II.1.1.1.) ityevamādīnāṃ svādhyāyavidhigrahaṇānyathānupapattyā prayojanavadarthaparatve kalpanīye śabdabhāvanetikartavyatāṃśasākāṃkṣasya vidheḥ sampradānabhūtadevatādistutidvāreṇa tadaṃśapūrakatvān naṣṭāśvadagdharathanyāyena tadubhayaikavākyatā ity arthavādādhikaraṇe nirṇītam / vedāntavākyajanyajñānāc ca sākṣād eva paramānandaprāptir niḥśeṣaduḥkhanivṛttiś ca puruṣārtho labhyata iti nirākāṃkṣatvān nānyaśeṣatvasambhāvanā, pratyuta vidhaya evāntaḥkaraṇaśuddhidvārā taccheṣatāṃ svata eva prāmāṇyād asty eva brahmeti na mīmāṃsakamatasiddhiḥ / tārkikādīnāṃ ca mataṃ "tat tvam asi" (ChU VI.8.7.), "ahaṃ brahmāsmi" (BAU I.4.10.), "ayam ātmā brahma" (BAU II.5.19.), "satyaṃ jñānaṃ anantaṃ brahma" (TU II.1.) ityādiśrutibādhitam, "ekam evādvitīyaṃ brahma" (ChU VI.2.1.), "neha nānāsti kiñcana" (BAU IV.4.19.) ityādiśrutibādhitaṃ ca / bhinnābhinnatvaṃ kṣaṇikatvaṃ ca "ākāśavat sarvagataś ca nityaḥ" ityādiśrutibādhitam / atra ca sarvaṣāṃ matasyāsattve pratijñāte viśuddhātmakatvād iti hetuḥ / nirvikalpakādvitīyacaitanyarūpatvād ity arthaḥ / atra hetuḥ viśiṣṭānubhūtyeti / viśiṣṭā savikalpakānubhūtibhyo vyāvṛttā yā tattvamasyādivākyajanyākhaṇḍānubhūtis tayety arthaḥ / tena sarvavyāpakam advitīyaṃ paramānandabodharūpaṃ ca brahmeti siddham // 4 //
body.translated_text: By the word 'etc.' (<s>ādi</s>), those not [explicitly] mentioned are included. First, insentient [matter] is not the material cause of the universe, because of the <s>śruti</s> declaring creation preceded by deliberation: 'It thought, may I become many, may I be born' (ChU VI.2.3); because of the designation of it as the <s>jīvātman</s> (individual self): 'Having entered through this living self, let me differentiate names and forms' (ChU VI.3.2); because of the promise that through knowing one thing, all this becomes known: 'By which, when known, all this becomes known' (MU I.1.3) — and through knowledge of <s>pradhāna</s>, the souls which are not its modifications cannot be known; and because of the teaching of non-difference from that, repeated nine times: 'All this has That as its self; That is the truth; He is the self; that thou art' (ChU VI.8.7); and because from another <s>śruti</s>, 'From this very self, space was born' (TU II.1), if something insentient were the cause of the universe, the varied design [of the world] would be inexplicable; and because <s>pradhāna</s>, <s>mahat</s>, etc. are without scriptural authority — therefore the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> view is not correct. Similarly, the <s>Pāśupata</s>, <s>Pāñcarātrika</s>, and <s>Jaina</s> views are untenable because they are contradicted by <s>śruti</s> and reasoning. Nor is the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> view correct that <s>śruti</s> does not teach <s>Brahman</s> because it is subsidiary to injunctions — since the subsidiarity to injunctions is unestablished. Nor can subsidiarity be established from the <s>arthavāda-adhikaraṇa</s> principle, because of dissimilarity. For those [passages] like 'Wind is the swiftest deity' (TS II.1.1.1), which do not themselves convey a purposeful meaning, when they are to be construed as conveying purposeful meaning through the impossibility of being otherwise [explained] except by the injunction of self-study (<s>svādhyāyavidhi</s>) — since they supplement the injunction's need for a recipient deity through praise of the deity, etc., by the maxim of 'the lost horse and the burnt chariot,' they form a single sentence — this has been determined in the <s>Arthavāda-adhikaraṇa</s>. And since from <s>Vedānta</s>-sentence-born knowledge, the supreme bliss is directly attained and the complete cessation of all suffering is [also] the goal of life — because of being self-sufficient, there is no possibility of its being subsidiary to anything else; rather, injunctions themselves are subsidiary to it through the purification of the inner organ. And from its own intrinsic validity, <s>Brahman</s> certainly exists — thus the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> position is not established. And the views of the <s>Tārkikas</s> and others are contradicted by <s>śrutis</s> such as 'That thou art' (ChU VI.8.7), 'I am <s>Brahman</s>' (BĀU I.4.10), 'This self is <s>Brahman</s>' (BĀU II.5.19), '<s>Brahman</s> is truth, knowledge, infinite' (TU II.1); and also by <s>śrutis</s> such as '<s>Brahman</s> is one only, without a second' (ChU VI.2.1), 'There is no diversity here whatsoever' (BĀU IV.4.19). And the views of difference-and-non-difference and momentariness are contradicted by <s>śrutis</s> such as 'Like space, all-pervading and eternal.' Here, when the invalidity of all [other] views has been declared, the reason given is 'because of being of pure nature' — meaning: because of being of the nature of non-conceptual, non-dual consciousness. The evidence for this reason is 'through a special experience' — meaning: through the indivisible experience (<s>akhaṇḍānubhūti</s>) born of sentences such as 'tat tvam asi' (That thou art), which is distinguished from [ordinary] conceptual experiences. Therefore it is established that <s>Brahman</s> is all-pervading, non-dual, and of the nature of supreme bliss and consciousness. // 4 //

body.text: nanu, "sa ya eṣo 'ṇimā" (ChU VI.8.15.), "aṇor aṇīyān" (TA X.12.1, KU I.2.20, SvU III.20.) iti brahmaṇo 'ṇutvaśruteḥ, "aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣaḥ" (KU II.4.12.), "ārāgramātro hy avaro 'pi dṛṣṭaḥ" (SvU V.8.) ityādiśrutipratipāditāṇujīvābhinnatvāc ca na brahmaṇaḥ sarvavyāpakatvam ity āśaṅkya "brahmaivedam amṛtaṃ purastāt brahma paścāt brahma dakṣiṇataś cottareṇa / adhaś cordhvaṃ ca prasṛtaṃ brahmaivedaṃ viśvam idaṃ variṣṭham" (MU II.2.11.), "tad etad brahmāpūrvam anaparam anantaram abāhyam" (BAU II.5.11.) ityādyāḥ śrutayo nirviśeṣam eva brahma pratipādayantīti pūrovoktam eva draḍhayann āha --
body.translated_text: Objection: Since there is a <s>śruti</s> teaching the atomic nature of <s>Brahman</s>: 'That which is this subtlety' (ChU VI.8.15), 'Subtler than the subtle' (TA X.12.1, KU I.2.20, ŚvU III.20); and since <s>Brahman</s> is non-different from the atomic <s>jīva</s> taught by <s>śrutis</s> such as 'The <s>puruṣa</s> of the measure of a thumb' (KU II.4.12), 'Even the minute one is seen to be of the measure of the tip of a goad' (ŚvU V.8) — <s>Brahman</s> is not all-pervading. Anticipating this, and in order to strengthen what was said before — that <s>śrutis</s> such as '<s>Brahman</s> is this immortal: <s>Brahman</s> in front, <s>Brahman</s> behind, <s>Brahman</s> to the south and north, spread below and above — this whole universe is <s>Brahman</s>, the greatest' (MU II.2.11); 'That <s>Brahman</s> is without before, without after, without inside, without outside' (BĀU II.5.11) — teach <s>Brahman</s> as entirely without distinctions — he says:

children.text: na cordhvaṃ na cādho na cāntar na bāhyaṃ na madhyaṃ na tiryaṅ na pūrvāparā dik /
children.translated_text: Not above, not below, not inside, not outside, not in the middle, not across, not in the eastern or western direction.

children.text: viyadvyāpakatvād akhaṇḍaikarūpas tad eko 'vaśiṣṭaḥ śivaḥ kevalo 'ham // 5 //
children.translated_text: Because of pervading space itself, [being] of one undivided form, That one alone remains — I am <s>Śiva</s>, the Absolute. // 5 //

body.text: ślokārthaḥ / viyadvyāpakatvāt viyadvad vyāpakatvāt "ākāśavat sarvagataś ca nitya" iti śruteḥ, viyato vyāpakatvād iti vā "jyāyān ākāśāt" (SatBr X.6.3.2), "mahato mayīyān" (KU II.20) ityādiśruteḥ / jīvasyāpi sakaladehavyāpicaitanyopalabdhyā mahattve 'pi, upādhidharmādhyāsenārāgramātratvābhidhānāt, "buddher guṇenātmaguṇena caiva hy ārāgramātro hy avaro 'pi dṛṣṭaḥ" (SvU V.8.) iti śruter brahmaṇaś ca sūkṣmatvābhiprāyeṇāṇutvavyapadeśāt / śeṣam atirohitārtham // 5 //
body.translated_text: Meaning of the verse: 'Because of being pervasive like space' — because of being pervasive in the manner of space, as the <s>śruti</s> says, 'Like space, all-pervading and eternal.' Or, 'because of being the pervader of space,' as the <s>śruti</s> says, 'Greater than space' (ŚatBr X.6.3.2) and 'Greater than the great' (KU II.20). Even though the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) also has greatness through the apprehension of consciousness pervading the entire body, because the attribution of being merely a needle-point is due to the superimposition of the properties of the limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>), as the <s>śruti</s> says: 'By the quality of the intellect and by the quality of the self, he is seen as smaller than the tip of a needle' (ŚvU V.8); and because the designation of <s>Brahman</s> as atomic is with the intention of subtlety. The rest is self-evident. // 5 //

body.text: nanu, brahmaṇo jagadupādānatvād upādānopādeyayoś cābhedād vicitrajagadabhinnatvena brahmaṇaḥ duḥkharūpatvāt na tadabhinnatvena jīvasya paramapuruṣārthaprāptir ity āśaṅkya brahmaṇaḥ svaprakāśaparamānandarūpatvān nikhilajagadbhramādhiṣṭhānatvena kāraṇatvavyapadeśād adhyastena ca samaṃ sambandhābhāvān na tatrānarthaleśo 'py astīty āha --
body.translated_text: Objection: Since <s>Brahman</s> is the material cause of the world, and since there is non-difference between the material cause and its effect, <s>Brahman</s> would be of the nature of suffering through being non-different from the variegated world, and therefore the <s>jīva</s> would not attain the supreme goal of life through being non-different from it. Anticipating this objection, [the author] says the following — since <s>Brahman</s> is of the nature of self-luminous supreme bliss, since it is designated as cause only by virtue of being the substratum of the illusion of the entire world, and since there is no relation whatsoever with what is superimposed, there is not the slightest trace of misfortune in it:

children.text: na śuklaṃ na kṛṣṇaṃ na raktaṃ na pītaṃ na kubjaṃ na pīnaṃ na hrasvaṃ na dīrgham /
children.translated_text: Not white, not black, not red, not yellow, not hunchbacked, not large, not short, not long,

children.text: arūpaṃ tathā jyotir ākārakatvāt tadeko 'vaśiṣṭaḥ śivaḥ kevalo 'ham // 6 //
children.translated_text: Formless, and of the nature of light, since it is self-illuminating — that one remaining, auspicious (<s>Śiva</s>), absolute — that am I. // 6 //

body.text: kubujam aṇu / pīnaṃ mahat / tenāṇu mahat hrasvaṃ dīrghaṃ ceti caturvidhaparimāṇaniṣedhāt dravyatvapratiṣedhaḥ / rūpyata iti rūpaṃ prameyam / na prameyaṃ arūpam / tena sarveṣām eva dravyaguṇakarmādipadārthānāṃ tattadvādyabhyupagatānāṃ niṣedhaḥ / tathā ca śrutiḥ "asthūlam anaṇv ahrasvam adīrgham alohitam" (BAU III.8.8.) ityādyāḥ "aśabdam asparśam arūpam avyayaṃ tathārasaṃ nityam agandhavac ca yat" (KathU I.3.15.) ityādyāś ca sarvānarthaśūnyaṃ paramātmasvarūpaṃ pratipādayanti / śrautasyāpy arthasya nyāyena nirṇayāya hetum āha -- jyotir ākārakatvād iti / svaprakāśajñānarūpatvenāprameyatvāt, prameyatve ghaṭādivajjaḍatvāpatteḥ, "etad aprameyaṃ dhruvam" (BAU IV.4.20.) ityādiśruteś cety arthaḥ // 6 //
body.translated_text: 'Hunchbacked' means minute (<s>aṇu</s>). 'Large' (<s>pīna</s>) means great (<s>mahat</s>). Thus, through the negation of the four types of magnitude — minute, great, short, and long — substance-hood is negated. 'That which is perceived' (<s>rūpyate</s>) is 'form' (<s>rūpa</s>), meaning 'knowable' (<s>prameya</s>). 'Not knowable' is 'formless' (<s>arūpa</s>). Thereby, all categories such as substance, quality, action, etc., as accepted by their respective proponents, are negated. And thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'Not gross, not minute, not short, not long, not red' (BAU III.8.8) etc. and 'That which is soundless, touchless, formless, imperishable, and likewise tasteless, eternal, and odorless' (KaU I.3.15) etc. — establish the nature of the supreme self as devoid of all affliction. He states the reason for determining even the scriptural meaning through reasoning — 'since it is of the nature of light,' meaning: because it is not knowable (<s>aprameya</s>) due to being of the nature of self-luminous knowledge; because if it were knowable, there would be the unwanted consequence of its being inert like a pot; and because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'This is the immeasurable, the permanent' (BAU IV.4.20). // 6 //

body.text: tṛtīyo vibhāgaḥ
body.translated_text: Third Division

body.text: tattvamasivākyārthanirṇayaḥ /
body.translated_text: Determination of the meaning of the sentence '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' (You are That)

body.text: nanu, kasya brahmabhāva upadiśyate, brahmaṇo 'brahmaṇo vā / nāntyaḥ, tasya jaḍatvād asattvāc ca, na prathamaḥ upadeśānarthakyāt, brahmabhāvasya svataḥsiddhatvāt / jīvasya svato brahmabhāve 'py avidyāvyavadhānaṃ jñānena nivartyata iti cet, na, avidyānivṛtter ātmabhinnatve dvaitāpatter brahmaṇo 'siddhiprasaṅgāt / tad uktaṃ vārtike (BAUBhV II.4.14.)
body.translated_text: Objection: Whose <s>Brahman</s>-hood is being taught — <s>Brahman</s>'s or non-<s>Brahman</s>'s? Not the latter, since it is inert and non-existent. Not the former, since the teaching would be purposeless, <s>Brahman</s>-hood being self-established. If [you say:] even though the <s>jīva</s> is inherently <s>Brahman</s>, the obstruction of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is removed by knowledge — no, because if the removal of <s>avidyā</s> were different from the self, there would be the unwanted consequence of duality and <s>Brahman</s> would not be established. This has been stated in the <s>Vārtika</s> (BAUBhV II.4.14):

children.text: "avyāvṛttānanugataṃ vastu brahmeti bhaṇyate /
children.translated_text: 'That reality which is unrestricted and all-pervading is called <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: brahmārtho durlabho 'tra syād dvitīye sati vastuni" // iti //
children.translated_text: The meaning of <s>Brahman</s> would be difficult to obtain if a second entity existed.' //

body.text: abhinnatve copadeśānarthakyam ity uktam / atra kiṃ paramārthataḥ phalābhāvam abhipraiṣi kiṃ vā pratītito 'pi / tatrādyam iṣṭāpattyā pariharati --
body.translated_text: It has been said that if [<s>Brahman</s> and <s>avidyā</s>-removal] are non-different, the teaching would be purposeless. Here, do you mean the absence of a result ultimately, or even phenomenally? Of these, the first is resolved through the welcome consequence (<s>iṣṭāpatti</s>):

children.text: na śāstā na śāstraṃ na śiṣyo na śikṣā na ca tvaṃ na cāhaṃ na cāyaṃ prapañcaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no teacher, no scripture, no student, no instruction, neither 'you' nor 'I,' nor this phenomenal world.

children.text: svarūpāvabodho vikalpāsahiṣṇus tad eko 'vaśiṣṭaḥ śivaḥ kevalo 'ham // 7 //
children.translated_text: The realization of one's own nature does not tolerate distinctions (<s>vikalpa</s>) — that one remaining, auspicious (<s>Śiva</s>), absolute — that am I. // 7 //

body.text: śāstā upadeśakartā guruḥ / śāstram upadeśakaraṇam / śiṣya upadeśakarma / śikṣā upadeśakriyā / tvaṃ śrotā / ahaṃ vaktā / ayaṃ sarvapramāṇasannidhāpitaḥ prapañco, dehendriyādir anarthaḥ, paramārthato nāstīty arthaḥ / dvitīyaṃ nirākaroti -- svarūpeti / ayam arthaḥ -- yady apy avidyānivṛttir ātmānātmā veti vikalpane kim api phalaṃ nirūpayituṃ na śakyate tathāpi svarūpāvabodho vijñānaphalam anubhūyate / na caitat katham iti vikalpanīyaṃ sarvadvaitopamardena vikalpāsahiṣṇutvāt / na hi dṛṣṭe 'nupapannaṃ nāma / tathā ca śrutiḥ (GauK II.32.)
body.translated_text: 'Teacher' (<s>śāstā</s>) is the giver of instruction, the <s>guru</s>. 'Scripture' (<s>śāstra</s>) is the instrument of instruction. 'Student' (<s>śiṣya</s>) is the object of instruction. 'Instruction' (<s>śikṣā</s>) is the act of teaching. 'You' is the hearer. 'I' is the speaker. 'This phenomenal world' (<s>prapañca</s>) — brought into view by all means of knowledge, comprising body, senses, etc., which is misfortune — does not exist ultimately; that is the meaning. [The author] removes the second [interpretation] with '<s>svarūpa</s>' (one's own nature). The meaning is this: although no result can be ascertained in the distinction 'self or not-self' [once <s>avidyā</s> is removed], nevertheless the realization of one's own nature is experienced as the fruit of knowledge (<s>vijñāna</s>). And this should not be questioned 'how is this possible,' since with the dissolution of all duality it does not tolerate distinctions. For what is directly experienced is never impossible. And thus the <s>śruti</s> (GauK II.32):

children.text: "na nirodho na cotpattir na baddho na ca sādhakaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'There is no cessation, no origination, no one in bondage, no aspirant,

children.text: na mumukṣur na vai mukta ity eṣā paramārthatā" //
children.translated_text: no seeker of liberation, and none liberated — this is the ultimate truth.' //

body.text: "brahma vā idam agra āsīt, tad ātmānam evāvedāhaṃ brahmāsmīti, tasmāt tatsarvam abhavat" (BAU I.4.7.) ityādyā pūrvam api brahmasvarūpasyaiva sato jīvasya jñānād brahmabhāvaṃ darśayati sarvaṃ ca dvaitaṃ vārayati // 7 //
body.translated_text: '<s>Brahman</s> indeed was this [universe] in the beginning; it knew only itself: I am <s>Brahman</s>; therefore it became all' (BAU I.4.7) — this and similar [<s>śrutis</s>] show that the <s>jīva</s>, who was already of the nature of <s>Brahman</s>, attains <s>Brahman</s>-hood through knowledge, and they negate all duality. // 7 //

body.text: nanv ātmanaḥ svaprakāśarūpatve sarvadā samāne jāgratsvapnasuṣuptyādivyavasthā katham / na ca bhrāntyaiva vyastheti vācyam, tathā sati sarvasyaiva svapnatvāpatter iti cet, na, lakṣaṇatas trayāṇām api svapnatve 'pi pratibhāsate 'vidyātmakaviśeṣasambhavād asadvilakṣaṇatvena tu saviśeṣatvād vyavasthopapatteḥ / paramārthatas tu kāpi vyavasthety āha --
body.translated_text: Objection: If the self-luminous nature of the self is always the same, how can the states of waking, dream, and deep sleep be explained? And one cannot say it is through delusion alone, for then the unwanted consequence would be that everything is a dream. Reply: No, because even though all three are dream-like in terms of their definition, since the peculiarity of <s>avidyā</s>-based appearance is possible, and since they are distinct from the non-existent by virtue of having characteristics, the distinction of states is justified. But ultimately, he says:

children.text: na jāgran na me svapnako vā suṣuptir na viśvo na vā taijasaḥ prājñako vā /
children.translated_text: For me there is no waking, no dream, nor deep sleep; I am not <s>Viśva</s> (the waking self), nor <s>Taijasa</s> (the dream self), nor <s>Prājña</s> (the deep sleep self).

children.text: avidyātmakatvāt trayāṇāṃ turīyas tad eko 'vaśiṣṭaḥ śivaḥ kevalo 'ham // 8 //
children.translated_text: Since all three are of the nature of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), I am the fourth (<s>Turīya</s>) — that one remaining, auspicious (<s>Śiva</s>), absolute — that am I. // 8 //

body.text: atra layakrameṇa paurvāparyayanirdeśaḥ / tathā hi -- asmanmate padārtho dvividhaḥ, dṛk dṛśyaś ca, anyavādiparikalpitānāṃ padārthānām atraivāntarbhāvāt / tatra dṛkpadārtha ātmā pāramārthika ekaḥ sarvadaikarupo 'py aupādhikabhedena trividhaḥ, īśvaro jīvaḥ sākṣī ceti / tatra kāraṇībhūtājñānopādhir īśvaraḥ, antaḥkaraṇatatsaṃskārāvacchinnājñānopahito jīvaḥ / prapañcitaṃ caitad adhastāt / avidyāpratibimbeśvarapakṣe bimbacaitanyaṃ, bimbeśvarapakṣe ca bimbapratibimbamukhānugatamukhasvarūpavaj jīveśvarānugataṃ sarvānusandhātṛ caitanyaṃ, sākṣīty ucyate / vārtikakāramate tv īśvara eva sākṣīti dvaividhyam eva jīveśvarabhedena dṣśaḥ / tatreśvaro 'pi trividhaḥ / svopādhibhūtāvidyāguṇatrayabhedena viṣṇukāraṇībhūtarajaupahito brahma sraṣṭā / hiraṇyagarbhas tu mahābhūtakāraṇatvābhāvān na brahmā tathāpi sthūlabhūtasraṣṭṛtvāt kvacid brahmety ucyate / kāraṇībhūtatamaupahito rudraḥ saṃhartā / evaṃ caikasyaiva caturbhujacaturmukhapañcamukhādyāḥ pumākārāḥ śrībhāratībhvānyādyāś ca stryākārāḥ / anye ca matsyakūrmādayo 'nantāvatārāḥ līlayaivāvirbhavanti bhaktānugrahārtham avadheyam,
body.translated_text: Here the enumeration follows the order of dissolution. Thus: in our doctrine, categories are twofold — the seer (<s>dṛk</s>) and the seen (<s>dṛśya</s>), since the categories postulated by other schools are included within these. Therein, the seer-category, the <s>Ātman</s>, though ultimately one and always of one form, is threefold through difference of limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>): <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), <s>jīva</s> (the individual soul), and <s>sākṣin</s> (the witness). Therein, <s>Īśvara</s> is conditioned by causal <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) as his limiting adjunct; the <s>jīva</s> is conditioned by ignorance delimited by the inner organ and its impressions. This has been elaborated below. In the view that <s>Īśvara</s> is the reflection of <s>avidyā</s>, the original consciousness is [the <s>sākṣin</s>]; in the view that <s>Īśvara</s> is the original, the consciousness that pervades both — like the original face that is reflected in both the face and its reflection — pervading both <s>jīva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s>, the witness of all mental operations, is called <s>sākṣin</s>. In the view of the author of the <s>Vārtika</s>, however, <s>Īśvara</s> alone is the <s>sākṣin</s>, so the division is only twofold: <s>jīva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s>. Therein, <s>Īśvara</s> too is threefold, according to the three <s>guṇas</s> of <s>avidyā</s> that constitute his limiting adjunct: <s>Viṣṇu</s> the creator (<s>Brahmā</s>), conditioned by causal <s>rajas</s>. <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, though not <s>Brahmā</s> in the strict sense since he is not the cause of the gross elements, is sometimes called <s>Brahmā</s> since he creates gross objects. <s>Rudra</s> the destroyer, conditioned by causal <s>tamas</s>. Thus, from the single [<s>Brahman</s>], the male forms such as four-armed [<s>Viṣṇu</s>], four-faced [<s>Brahmā</s>], five-faced [<s>Śiva</s>], etc., and the female forms such as <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Bhāratī</s>, <s>Bhavānī</s>, etc., arise. And other countless incarnations such as <s>Matsya</s>, <s>Kūrma</s>, etc. manifest through <s>līlā</s> (divine play) for the grace of devotees — this should be noted.

children.text: "cinmayasyādvitīyasya niṣkalasyāśarīriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For the one who is of the nature of consciousness, non-dual, without parts, and bodiless,

children.text: upāsakānāṃ kāryārthaṃ brahmaṇo rūpakalpanā //" iti śruteḥ //
children.translated_text: the form of <s>Brahman</s> is imagined for the sake of the goal of worshippers' — thus says the <s>śruti</s>. //

body.text: jīvo' pi trividhaḥ, svopādhyavāntarabhedena viśvataijasaprājñabhedāt / tatrāvidyāntaḥkaraṇasthūlaśarīrāvacchinno jāgradavasthābhimānī viśvaḥ / sa eva sthūlaśarīrābhimānarahita upādhidvayopahitaḥ svapnābhimānī taijasaḥ / śarīrāntaḥkaraṇopādhidvayarahito 'ntaḥkaraṇasaṃskārāvacchinnāvidyāmātropahitaḥ suṣuptyabhimānī prājñaḥ / eteṣāṃ ca svatantropādhibhedābhāvena svatantrabhedābhāve 'py avāntaropādhibhedād ekatve 'py avāntarabhedo vyahahriyate / sākṣī tu sarvānusandhātā sarvānugatas turīyākhya ekavidha eva / tatropādhibhedenāpi na kvacid bhedas tadupādher ekarūpatvāt / avidyātadvyāpyatatkāryātmakaḥ prapañco dṛṣyapadārthaḥ / tasya cāpāramārthikatve 'pi vyāvahārikasattvābhyupagamāt na svāpnikapadārthavan nirūpaṇaṃ vyartham, upāsanādāv upayogād iti / so 'pi trividhaḥ avyākṛtāmūrtamūrtabhedāt / tatra sābhāsāvidyā mūrtāmūrtaprapañcabījaśaktirūpā tadajanyatve 'pi tannivṛttau nirvartamānatvena tadvyāpyaiś caitanyatatsambandhajīveśvaravibhāgacidābhāsaiḥ sahānāditvād avyākṛtam ity ucyate / sā ca svayaṃ jaḍāpy ajaḍena cidābhāsenojjvalitapūrvapūrvasaṃskārajīvakarmaprayuktā satī śabdasparśarūparasagandhātmakāny ākāśavāyutejojalapṛthivyākhyāni pañcamahābhūtāni janayati / tatra pūrvapūrvabhūtabhāvāpannāyā avidyāyā uttarottaraṃ prati kāraṇatvāt pūrvapūrvabhūtaguṇānām uttarottarabhuteṣv anupreveśaḥ / evam avidyāta evāndhakāro 'pi bhāvarūpa evāvaṇātmā cākṣuṣajñānavirodhī ālokanāśyaś ca jhaṭiti mahāvidyudādivad āvirbhavati tirobhavati ceti siddhāntaḥ / saṃsārahetudehopādanatvābhāvāc ca śrutiṣu sṛṣṭiprakriyāyām āmnāyata ity avirodhaḥ / dikkālau tv aprāmāṇikatvān noktau, ākāśasyaiva digvyavahārajanakatvavyavasthāsambhavāt "diśaḥ śrotram" (BAU III.2.13.) iti śruteś ca / kālas tv avidyaiva tasyā eva sarvādhāratvād iti / ayaṃ cāvyākṛtapadārtha īśvaropādhiḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>jīva</s> (individual self) is also threefold, due to the subsidiary distinctions of its own limiting adjuncts, being divided into <s>Viśva</s>, <s>Taijasa</s>, and <s>Prājña</s>. Among these: the one delimited by <s>avidyā</s>, the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> (inner organ), and the gross body, who identifies with the waking state, is <s>Viśva</s>. That same [self], free from identification with the gross body but conditioned by the two adjuncts [of avidyā and antaḥkaraṇa], who identifies with the dream state, is <s>Taijasa</s>. Free from both adjuncts of body and antaḥkaraṇa, conditioned solely by <s>avidyā</s> delimited by the impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>, who identifies with the state of deep sleep, is <s>Prājña</s>. Although these have no independent distinction — due to the absence of independent differences in their limiting adjuncts — the subsidiary distinction is spoken of even within their unity, due to the subsidiary differences of the adjuncts. The witness (<s>sākṣin</s>), however — the one who cognizes all, who pervades all, called the Fourth (<s>turīya</s>) — is of one kind only. In it, there is no differentiation even through differences in limiting adjuncts, since its adjunct is of one single nature. The phenomenal world (<s>prapañca</s>), consisting of <s>avidyā</s>, that which is pervaded by it, and its effects — is the object of perception (<s>dṛśya</s>). Although it is not ultimately real, since its empirical reality (<s>vyāvahārika-sattva</s>) is accepted, its analysis is not useless — unlike dream objects — because it is useful in meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>) and the like. It too is threefold: the unmanifest (<s>avyākṛta</s>), the formless (<s>amūrta</s>), and the formed (<s>mūrta</s>). There, <s>avidyā</s> together with its reflection [of consciousness] — being the seed-power of the formed and formless phenomenal world, and though not produced by them, being removed when they are removed — together with consciousness, the reflections of consciousness that constitute the distinction of <s>jīva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s>, and their connections, being beginningless — is called the 'unmanifest' (<s>avyākṛta</s>). And it, though itself inert, being illuminated by the non-inert reflection of consciousness, prompted by the <s>karmas</s> of the <s>jīva</s> [arising] from accumulated prior impressions, generates the five great elements — <s>ākāśa</s> (space), <s>vāyu</s> (air), <s>tejas</s> (fire), <s>jala</s> (water), and <s>pṛthivī</s> (earth) — whose natures are sound, touch, form, taste, and smell respectively. Since the <s>avidyā</s> that has assumed the form of each preceding element is the cause with respect to each succeeding one, the qualities of the preceding elements enter into the succeeding ones. Likewise, darkness too arises from <s>avidyā</s> alone, is a positive entity, is of the nature of concealment (<s>āvaraṇa</s>), opposes visual cognition, is destroyed by light, and appears and disappears suddenly like great lightning — this is the established doctrine. And since there is no contradiction with its being taught in the scriptural creation-process, because it lacks the status of being the material cause of the body which is the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Space (<s>dik</s>) and time (<s>kāla</s>) are not separately mentioned, since they lack independent authority as means of knowledge — because it is possible to establish that <s>ākāśa</s> itself gives rise to the usage of directions, and because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'The directions are the ear' (BĀU III.2.13). Time, however, is <s>avidyā</s> itself, since it alone is the substratum of everything. This unmanifest category is the limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) of <s>Īśvara</s>.

body.text: tāni ca sūkṣmāṇy apy apañcīkṛtāni pañcamahābhūtāny amūrtākhyāni kāraṇaikyāt sattvarajastamoguṇātmakāni sattvāṃśaprādhānyena jñānakriyāśaktipradhānāṃśaḥ prāṇaḥ / sa ca pañcadhā, prāṇo 'pāṇo vyāna udānaḥ samāna iti / evam ekaikabhutebhyo jñānakriyāśaktibhedāt pratyekam indriyadvayaṃ jāyate / ākāśāc chrotravācau, vāyos tvakpāṇī, tejasaś cakṣuḥpādau, adbhyo rasanapāyū, pṛthivyā ghrāṇopasthau ceti / atra "tajomayī vāk" (ChU VI.5.4.) iti śrutes taijasī vāk, pādas tu nābhasa iti kecit / śabdavyañjakendriyatvena tu śrotravadvāco nābhasatvam, pādacikitsayā ca cakṣuṣaḥ svāsthyadarśanāc cakṣurvat pādasyāpi taijasatvam iti tu yuktam utpaśyāmaḥ / tejomayatvaśrutis tu manasaḥ pañcabhūtakāryasyāpi annamayatvaśrutir iva tadupakāryatayā vyākhyeyā / manasaś ca pañcabhūtaguṇagrāhakatvena tadvattvaniścayāt pañcabhūtātmakatvam ity anyad etat / eteṣām adhiṣṭhātāro devā api jñānakriyāśaktipradhānāḥ, digagnī, vātendrau, ādityaviṣṇū, varunamitrau, aśviprajāpatī / tatra jñānaśaktisamaṣṭir antaḥkaraṇaṃ, kriyāśaktisamaṣṭiḥ prāṇaḥ / śabdasparśarūpasaragandhagrāhakāṇi śrotratvakcakṣūrasanaghrāṇākhyāni pañcajñānendriyāṇi / tvakcakṣuṣī svahrāhyaguṇāśrayadravyam api gṛhṇītaḥ / śrotram api cakṣurvat gattvā śabdagrāhakam dūre śabda iti pratyayāt / vacanādanāgativisargānandajanakāni vākyāṇipādapāyūpasthākhyāni pañcakarmendriyāṇi / etac ca sarvaṃ militvā saptadaśakaṃ liṅgaṃ jñānaśaktiprādhānyena hiraṇyagarbha iti kriyāśaktiprādhānyena sūtram iti cocyate / ayam amūrtapadārthaḥ kāryatvāt vyaṣṭau samaṣṭau ca jīvopādhir eva /
body.translated_text: Those same five great elements, though subtle and not yet quintupled, being called 'formless' (<s>amūrta</s>), are composed of the three <s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — due to the unity of their cause. From the predominance of the <s>sattva</s> portion, the aspect predominating in the powers of knowledge and action is <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath). It is fivefold: <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, <s>vyāna</s>, <s>udāna</s>, and <s>samāna</s>. Likewise, from each element, due to the distinction between the powers of knowledge and action, a pair of sense-organs is born from each: from <s>ākāśa</s> — the ear and speech; from <s>vāyu</s> — the skin and hands; from <s>tejas</s> — the eye and feet; from water — the tongue and the organ of excretion; from earth — the nose and the organ of generation. Here, some hold that speech is of fire, based on the <s>śruti</s> 'Speech is made of fire' (ChU VI.5.4), while the feet belong to space. But we consider it reasonable that speech, being the organ that manifests sound, belongs to space like the ear; and that the feet, like the eye, belong to fire — since by treating the feet, one observes the restoration of sight. The <s>śruti</s> declaring speech to be 'made of fire' should be explained as [indicating] its being assisted by fire, just as the <s>śruti</s> declaring even the mind — which is a product of all five elements — to be 'made of food' [indicates assistance]. And since the mind's grasping of the qualities of all five elements establishes its nature as composed of all five elements — this is a different matter. The presiding deities of these [sense-organs], also predominating in the powers of knowledge and action, are: the Directions and <s>Agni</s>; <s>Vāyu</s> and <s>Indra</s>; <s>Āditya</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>; <s>Varuṇa</s> and <s>Mitra</s>; the <s>Aśvins</s> and <s>Prajāpati</s>. The aggregate of the powers of knowledge is the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> (inner organ); the aggregate of the powers of action is <s>prāṇa</s>. The five organs of knowledge — ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose — grasp sound, touch, form, taste, and smell respectively. Skin and eye also grasp the substance that is the substratum of the quality they grasp. The ear too, like the eye, grasps sound by going [toward it] — since we have the cognition 'the sound is far away.' The five organs of action — speech, hands, feet, the organ of excretion, and the organ of generation — produce, respectively, utterance, grasping, movement, discharge, and pleasure. All of these combined form the seventeen-fold <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body), which, insofar as the power of knowledge predominates, is called <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (the Golden Embryo), and insofar as the power of action predominates, is called <s>Sūtra</s> (the Thread-self). This 'formless' category, being an effect, serves as the limiting adjunct of the <s>jīva</s> both individually and collectively.

body.text: tāni ca tathābhūtāni bhūtāni bhogāyatanaṃ śarīraṃ bhogyaṃ ca viṣayam antareṇa bhogaṃ janayitum aśaknuvanti jīvakarmaprayuktatvāt sthaulyāya pañcīkṛtāni bhavanti / tatra ca pratyekaṃ pañcabhūtāni dvidhā vibhajyate / tatra ekaiko bhāgaś caturdhā vibhajyate / tadbhāgacatuṣṭayaṃ ca svabhāvaṃ vihāya itarabhūtacatuṣṭayārdhabhāgeṣu praviśati iti svasyārdhabhāgenetareṣām aṣṭmabhāgena ca pañcīkaraṇān melane 'py ādhikyād ākāśādiśabdaprayogaḥ /
body.translated_text: Those elements in their [subtle] form, being unable to generate the body — which is the seat of experience (<s>bhogāyatana</s>) — and the objects of experience, without which experience cannot arise, and being prompted by the <s>karmas</s> of the <s>jīva</s>, become 'quintupled' (<s>pañcīkṛta</s>) for the purpose of grossness. In this process, each of the five elements is divided in two. One half of each is divided into four parts. Those four parts, leaving their own nature, enter into the half-portions of the other four elements. Thus, through quintuplication, even in the combination [of elements], due to the predominance [of each element in its own product], the designation as '<s>ākāśa</s>' etc. [is used].

body.text: atra "trivṛtaṃ trivṛtam ekaikāṃ karavāṇi" (ChU VI.3.3.) iti śruteḥ "trivṛtkurvata upadeśāt" (BS II.4.20.) iti sūtrāc ca trayāṇām eva melanapratīteś ca trivṛtkaraṇam eva kecin manyante te viyadadhikaraṇānyāyenaiva nirākṛtāḥ / tathā hi taittirīyake "tasmād vā etasmād ātmana ākāśaḥ sambhūtaḥ, ākāśād vāyuḥ" (TU II.1.1.) ityādiśruteḥ chāndogye ca trayāṇāṃ tejobannānāṃ sṛṣṭiśravaṇe 'pi dvayor upasaṃhāraḥ, tejasaḥ prāthamyapadārthadharmāpekṣayā ākāśavāyupadārthayor balīyastvāt, chāndogye caikavijñānena sarvavijñānapratijñānāt, ākāśavāyvor acetanayor brahmakāryatvasyāvaśyaṃ vācyatvāt / tatra pañcānām eva melane 'py avayutyānuvādena trivṛtkaraṇopapattiḥ / trivṛtam eveti tu kalpanāyāṃ vākyabhedaprasaṅgaḥ / "trivṛtkurvata upadeśāt" (BS II.4.20.) iti sūtraṃ tv anuvādakatvān na pañcīkaraṇaṃ nyāyasiddhaṃ bādhitum utsahate / melanapratītiś ca śarīrādau pañcānām aviśiṣṭaiva, pañcīkṛtapañcamahābhūtānīti ca bhāṣyakāravacanam / tasmād akam anenānātmacintaneneti dik /
body.translated_text: Here, some hold that only triplication (<s>trivṛtkaraṇa</s>) [occurs], based on the <s>śruti</s> 'Let me make each one triple' (ChU VI.3.3), the <s>sūtra</s> 'Because of the teaching to make triple' (BS II.4.20), and the observed combination of only three [elements]. They are refuted by the reasoning [applied to] the <s>viyadadhikaraṇa</s> (the section on space). For in the <s>Taittirīya</s> [Upaniṣad], the <s>śruti</s> 'From that very self, space was born; from space, air' (TU II.1.1) etc. teaches [the creation of five elements]; and in the <s>Chāndogya</s>, even though only the creation of the three — fire, water, and food — is heard, the other two are subsumed, since the content-nature of the terms <s>ākāśa</s> and <s>vāyu</s>, being stronger [in authority], takes precedence over the property-nature of fire's primacy; and since the <s>Chāndogya</s> promises 'by knowing one, all becomes known'; and since the statement that <s>ākāśa</s> and <s>vāyu</s>, being non-conscious, are products of <s>Brahman</s>, must necessarily be made. In the quintuplication of all five, triplication is also accounted for through restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) of the main [elements]. But restricting it to triplication alone would occasion a split in the [unity of the] sentence. The <s>sūtra</s> 'Because of the teaching to make triple' (BS II.4.20), being a restatement, is not capable of overriding quintuplication, which is established by reasoning. And the observed combination in bodies etc. pertains equally to all five [elements]. The <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (<s>Śaṅkara</s>) also says 'the quintupled five great elements.' Therefore, enough of this fruitless speculation — this is the gist.

body.text: tāni ca pañcīkṛtāni pañcamahābhūtāni mūrtākhyāni militvā ekaṃ kāryam indriyāṇām adhiṣṭhānaṃ bhogāyatanam utpādayanti / tad eva śarīram ity ucyate / tatra sattvapradhānaṃ devaśarīraṃ, rajaḥpradhānaṃ manuṣyaśarīraṃ, tamaḥpradhānaṃ tiryagādisthāvarāntaṃ śarīram / tasya ca śarīrasya pāñcabhautikasyāpi citrarūpasyeva kvacin nyūnādhikabhāvo bhūtānāṃ na virudhyate / evaṃ viṣayā api pañcīkṛtaikaikabhūtajanyāś caturdaśabhuvanākhyā ūrdhvamadhyādhobhāvena sattvarajastamoṃśapradhānāḥ ghaṭādayaś ca / etat sarvaṃ brahmāṇḍākhyaṃ virāḍ iti mūrtam iti cocyate /
body.translated_text: Those quintupled five great elements, called 'formed' (<s>mūrta</s>), combine to produce the one effect that is the seat of the sense-organs, the locus of experience. This is called the 'body' (<s>śarīra</s>). Among these: a body in which <s>sattva</s> predominates is a divine body; one in which <s>rajas</s> predominates is a human body; one in which <s>tamas</s> predominates is the body of animals, ending with immovable [plants]. And even though the body is composed of all five elements, just as with a variegated picture, the excess or deficiency of elements in different [bodies] is not contradictory. Likewise, objects of experience too — produced from each quintupled element individually, called the fourteen worlds, arranged in upper, middle, and lower regions, predominating in <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> portions respectively — as well as pots and the like. All this together, called the <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s> (cosmic egg), is designated as <s>Virāj</s> and as the 'formed' (<s>mūrta</s>).

body.text: ayam aupaniṣadaḥ sṛṣṭikramaḥ / tadviparīto layakramaḥ / pañcīkṛtapañcamahābhūtatatkāryātmakaṃ virāḍākhyaṃ mūrtaṃ pṛthivyādhyekaikabhūtalayenāmūrte 'pañcīkṛtapañcamahābhūtātmake hiraṇyagarbhākhye svakāraṇe līyate / sa eva dainandinaḥ pralayaḥ / amūrtaṃ cāvyākṛte parameśvaropādhau / avyākṛtasya tv anāditvena kāraṇābhāvān na layaḥ, svakāraṇe sūkṣmarūpeṇāvasthānaṃ laya iti tallakṣaṇāt / ayam eva prākṛtaḥ pralayaḥ / brahmajñānād ātyantika ucchedas tu ātyantikaḥ pralayaḥ / sa ca kāraṇakrameṇaiva, kāraṇocchedād eva kāryocchedāt / sarvaṃ ca sṛṣṭipralayādikaṃ svapnasṛṣṭipralayavad apāramārthikam api vāsanādārḍhyāt vyavahārakṣamam iti na māyikatve 'pi tucchatvaprasaṅgaḥ / yathā caitat tathā vyaktam ākare /
body.translated_text: This is the order of creation according to the <s>Upaniṣads</s>. The order of dissolution is the reverse. The 'formed' (<s>mūrta</s>), called <s>Virāj</s>, consisting of the quintupled five great elements and their effects, dissolves — through the successive dissolution of each element beginning with earth — into the 'formless' (<s>amūrta</s>), consisting of the unquintupled five great elements, called <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, which is its cause. This is the daily dissolution (<s>dainandinaḥ pralayaḥ</s>). The formless [dissolves] into the unmanifest (<s>avyākṛta</s>), which is the limiting adjunct of the Supreme Lord. But the unmanifest, being beginningless, has no cause and hence no dissolution — since dissolution is defined as the subsistence in subtle form within one's own cause. This is the natural dissolution (<s>prākṛtaḥ pralayaḥ</s>). The absolute cessation through the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> is the final dissolution (<s>ātyantikaḥ pralayaḥ</s>). And this [occurs] only through the order of causes — since the cessation of effects [follows] only from the cessation of causes. And all creation, dissolution, and the like, though not ultimately real — like creation and dissolution in a dream — are capable of transactional validity due to the firmness of impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>). Hence, there is no unwelcome consequence of utter unreality even in their being illusory (<s>māyika</s>). How all this is so is made clear in the [original] source text.

body.text: evaṃ sthite jāgaraṇādivyavasthocyate / indriyavṛttikālīnārthopalambho jāgaraṇam / tatra ca mūrtaṃ virāḍākhyaṃ bhogyaṃ pratyakṣādipramāṇaṣaṭkena vyavahriyamāṇatvāt vyāvahārikaṃ viśvākhyena jīvenopabhujyate / sa ca dehendriyādiṣu praveśāt vyāpanād vā viśva ity ucyate, viśa praveśane viṣ.l vyāptāv iti ca smaraṇāt / atra yady api viśvenāmūrtam avyākṛtaṃ cānumānādinānubhūyate, tathāpi vyāvahārikaṃ sarvaṃ viśvenaiva jñāyata iti niyamāt sthūlaśarīropādhyabhimānitvāc ca na tasya avasthāntaravyāpakatvam / śuktirajatādijñānānām aprāmāṇikatvāt tadviṣayasyāvyāvahārikatve 'pi indriyavyāpārakālīnatvāj jāgaraṇopapattiḥ / jñānotpattyādiprakriyā cādhastād uktaiva /
body.translated_text: This being established, the arrangement of the waking state and the like is now described. Waking (<s>jāgaraṇa</s>) is the apprehension of objects concurrent with the operation of the sense organs. In that state, the embodied (<s>mūrta</s>) [reality] called <s>Virāj</s>, being the object of experience, since it is dealt with through the six means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) such as perception, is empirically real (<s>vyāvahārika</s>) and is experienced by the <s>jīva</s> called <s>Viśva</s>. And he is called <s>Viśva</s> because of entering into or pervading the body, senses, and the like — since the root <s>viś</s> means 'to enter' and <s>viṣ.l</s> means 'to pervade.' Here, although the <s>Viśva</s> also experiences the formless (<s>amūrta</s>) and the unmanifest (<s>avyākṛta</s>) through inference and the like, nevertheless, since there is the rule that everything empirically real is known by the <s>Viśva</s> alone, and since it identifies with the gross body as its limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>), it does not pervade the other states. The waking state is justified even for the cognitions of shell-silver and the like — though their objects are not empirically real, since they are not produced by valid means of knowledge — because they occur during the operation of the sense organs. And the procedure of the origination of knowledge and the like has already been stated above.

body.text: evaṃ jāgrabhogajanakakarmakṣaye svāpnabhogajanakakarmodaye ca sati nirākhyayā tāmasyā vṛttyā sthūladehābhimāne dūrīkṛtte sarvendriyeṣu devatānugrahābhāvān nirvyāpāratayā līneṣu viśvo 'pi līna ity ucyate / tadā ca svapnāvasthā / tatrāntaḥkaraṇavāsanānimitta indriyavṛttyabhāvakālīno 'rthopalambhaḥ svapnaḥ / tatra ca mana eva gajaturagādyarthākāreṇa vivartate avidyāvṛttyā ca jñāyata iti kecit / avidyaiva śuktirajatādivat svapnārthakāreṇa pariṇamate jñāyate cāvidyāvṛttyety anye / kaḥ pakṣaḥ śreyān? uttaraḥ / avidyāyā eva sarvatrārthādhyāsajñānādhyāsopādānatvena kalpitatvān manogatavāsanānimittatvena ca kvacin manaḥpariṇāmatvavyapadeśāt / nanu, tadā manaso dṛśyākārapariṇāmānabhyupagame dṛṣṭṛtvasambhavenātmanaḥ svayaṃjyotiṣṭ.vāsiddhir iti cet, na, bahirindriyajanyavṛttyabhāvena tadānīṃ manaso'grāhakatvāt tatsahakāreṇaiva tasya grāhakatvaniyamāt, savṛttikāntaḥkaraṇāvacchinnasyaiva caitanyasya pramātṛtvaniyamāt tadāntaḥkaranasattve 'pi pramātrabhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus, when the <s>karma</s> that generates the enjoyments of the waking state is exhausted and the <s>karma</s> that generates the enjoyments of the dream state arises, when the identification with the gross body is set aside by a <s>tāmasa</s> (dark/ignorance-based) mental modification that has no name, and when all the sense organs are merged into inactivity due to the absence of divine favor, the <s>Viśva</s> too is said to be merged. Then comes the dream state (<s>svapnāvasthā</s>). In it, the dream is the apprehension of objects caused by the impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) in the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), concurrent with the absence of sense-organ operation. Some say: the mind itself transforms (<s>vivartate</s>) into the form of objects such as elephants and horses, and is known through a modification of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). Others say: <s>avidyā</s> itself transforms into the form of dream-objects, like shell-silver and the like, and is known through a modification of <s>avidyā</s>. Which view is better? The latter. Because <s>avidyā</s> alone, being everywhere the material cause of both the superimposition of objects and the superimposition of cognition, is posited [as such]; and the designation 'transformation of the mind' is used only in some cases because of the impressions in the mind serving as the occasioning cause. Objection: If the mind's transformation into the form of the visible is not accepted, then since the self could be the seer, the self's self-luminosity would not be established. Reply: No, because at that time the mind, in the absence of a modification produced by the external senses, is not capable of apprehension, since there is a rule that its apprehending capacity depends on the cooperation of those [external senses]; and since there is a rule that only consciousness delimited by the inner organ accompanied by a modification has the status of a knower — even when the inner organ exists [in dreams], there is no knower-status [without the external senses].

body.text: kimadhiṣṭhānaṃ svapnādhyāsasya manovacchinnaṃ jīvacaitanyam ity eke, mūlājñānāvacchinnaṃ brahmacaitanyam ity apare / kiṃ śreyaḥ? matabhedenobhayam api / tathā hi -- jāgradbodhena svapnabhramanivṛttyabhyupagamād adhiṣṭhānajñānād eva ca bhramanivṛtteḥ, brahmacaitanyasya cādhiṣṭhānatve saṃsāradaśāyāṃ tajjñānatvābhāvāt jñānena ca sarvadvaitanivṛtteḥ na jāgradbodhāt svapnanivṛttiḥ syāt / "sa hi kartā" (BAU IV.3.10.) iti ca jīvakartṛtvaśruteḥ ākāśādiprapañcavat sarvasādhāraṇyāpatteś ca na mūlājñānāvacchinnaṃ brahmacaitanyam adhiṣṭhānam /
body.translated_text: What is the substratum (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) of dream superimposition? Some say: the <s>jīva</s>-consciousness delimited by the mind. Others say: <s>Brahman</s>-consciousness delimited by root ignorance (<s>mūlājñāna</s>). Which is preferable? According to the difference of doctrinal positions, both. For if it is accepted that dream-error is removed by waking cognition, and since error is removed only by knowledge of the substratum, and since — if <s>Brahman</s>-consciousness were the substratum — knowledge of it does not exist in the state of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and since knowledge [of <s>Brahman</s>] removes all duality, then dream would not be removed by waking cognition. And from the <s>śruti</s> "For he is the maker" (BAU IV.3.10), which declares the <s>jīva</s>'s agency, and because of the unwanted consequence that [dream] would be common to all [jīvas], like the phenomenal world of space and the like — <s>Brahman</s>-consciousness delimited by root ignorance is not the substratum.

body.text: nanu, jīvacaitanyasyānāvṛtttatvena sarvadābhāsamānatvāt katham adhiṣṭhānatvam? satyaṃ, tatrāpi svapnādhyāsānukūlavyāvahārikasaṃghātabhānavirodhyavasthājñānābhyupagamāt, svapnadaśāyāṃ cāhaṃ manuṣya ityādipratītikasaṃghātāntarabhānābhyupagamāt śayyāyāṃ svapimīti śayyāntaravat / bhānasāmagryabhāvaś ca tulya eva /
body.translated_text: Objection: Since <s>jīva</s>-consciousness is never concealed and always appears, how can it be the substratum [of error]? Reply: True, but because even there, a state-specific ignorance (<s>avasthājñāna</s>) is accepted that is opposed to the appearance of the empirically real aggregate [of waking experience] favorable to dream-superimposition; and because in the dream state, the appearance of another aggregate — as in the cognition 'I am a human being' etc. — is accepted, just as the bed [appears as something else] when one [dreams] 'I am sleeping on the bed.' And the absence of the totality of conditions for [waking] appearance is equal [in both cases].

body.text: nanu, ahaṃ manuṣya ityādivyāvahārikasaṃghātajñānasya pramāṇājanyatvāt katham ajñānanivartakatā / avasthāntarānyathānupapattyā tatkalpane suṣuptāv api svapnabādhakajñānam āsthīyeta, tac cāniṣṭaṃ jāgrattvāpatter iti cet, sādhv avocaḥ, svapnāvasthājñānasyaivāntaḥkaraṇalayasahitasya suṣuptirūpatvān na tatra tadbādhaḥ / jāgaraṇe tu mithyaiva svapno 'bhād ity anubhavād aham iti jñānasya pramāṇājanyatve 'pi yathārthatvāt śarīrādijñānasya ca pramāṇajanyatvād avasthājñānavirodhitvam anubhavasiddham / viśeṣājñānaṃ tu na pramāṇajanyavṛttim antareṇa nivartate / sākṣiṇaś cāvidyānivartakatvābhāvo 'vidyāsādhakatvenaiva dharmigrāhakamānasiddha iti na kiñcid avadyam / yāvanti jñānāni tāvanty ajñānānīti cābhyupagamāt śuktijñāneneva vyāvahārikasaṃghātajñānenājñānanivṛttāv api punar api kadācid rajatabhramavan na svapnādhyāsānupapattir iti jīvacaitanyam evādhiṣṭhānam iti pakṣe na ko 'pi doṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: Objection: Since the cognition of the empirically real aggregate 'I am a human being' and so forth is not produced by a means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), how can it remove ignorance? If state-specific ignorance is postulated on the ground that the other state cannot be explained otherwise, then even in deep sleep a cognition sublating dream should be posited — and that is undesirable, since it would entail the waking state [in deep sleep]. Reply: Well said. Since the state-specific ignorance of dream, accompanied by the dissolution of the inner organ, has the very form of deep sleep, there is no sublation of it [in deep sleep]. But in waking, from the experience 'the dream was indeed false,' even though the cognition 'I' is not produced by a means of knowledge, since it is veridical, and since the cognition of the body and the like is produced by a means of knowledge, its opposition to state-specific ignorance is established by experience. However, particular ignorances (<s>viśeṣājñāna</s>) are not removed without a mental modification produced by a valid means of knowledge. And the witness (<s>sākṣin</s>)'s inability to remove <s>avidyā</s> is established by the very same means of knowledge that apprehends the substrate, since it serves to establish <s>avidyā</s> [rather than remove it]. So there is no fault. And since it is accepted that there are as many ignorances as cognitions, even when ignorance is removed by the cognition of the empirically real aggregate — just as shell-knowledge [removes ignorance of the shell but silver-error can recur] — the superimposition of dream is not impossible, just as silver-error [can recur]. Therefore, in the view that <s>jīva</s>-consciousness alone is the substratum, there is no fault at all.

body.text: yadā punar brahmajñānād evājñānanivṛttyabhyupagamas tadā rajjvāṃ daṇḍabhrameṇa sarpabhramatirodhānavad adhiṣṭhānajñānābhāve 'pi jāgradbhrameṇa svapnabhramatirobhāvopapatteḥ brahmacaitanyam eva svapnādhyāsādhiṣṭhānam iti pakṣe 'pi na kaścid doṣaḥ / pratijīvaṃ svapnādhyāsāsādhāraṇyaṃ tu manogatavāsanānām asādhāraṇyād eva /
body.translated_text: When, however, the removal of <s>ajñāna</s> by <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge alone is accepted, then — just as the error of a serpent in a rope can be concealed by the error of a stick, even without knowledge of the substratum [rope] — so too the concealment of dream-error by waking-error is possible even without [waking] knowledge of the substratum. Therefore, in the view that <s>Brahman</s>-consciousness alone is the substratum of dream-superimposition, there is no fault either. And the individuality of dream-superimposition for each <s>jīva</s> is due to the individuality of the impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) residing in each mind.

body.text: manovacchinnaṃ brahmacaitanyam evādhiṣṭhānam etasminn api pakṣe 'vasthājñānasyāvarakatvāṅgīkārān na kāpy anupapattiḥ / ata eva śāstreṣu kvacit kvacit tathā vyapadeśaḥ / nanu, manovacchinnacaitanyasyādhiṣṭhānatve ahaṃ gaja ity āhaṅkārasāmānādhikaraṇyena gajapratītiḥ syāt idaṃ rajatam iti śuktisāmānādhikaraṇyena rajatapratītivat natv ayaṃ gaja iti / brahmacaitanyasyādhiṣṭhānatvapakṣe 'pi gaja ity ākārair eva pratītiḥ syān na tv ayaṃ gaja iti tatrāpīdaṅkārāspadībhūtabāgyārthābhāvasya samānatvād iti cet, na, ādye pakṣe ahaṅkārasya śuktivad adhiṣṭhānānavacchedakatvāt śuktī rajatam itivad ahaṃ gaja iti na bhramakāraprasaṅgaḥ / aham iti jñānasyeyaṃ śuktir iti jñānasyeva bhramavirodhitvāt, idamaṃśasya ca bhramāvirodhina eva tatra bhānābhyupagamāt / antye tu gaja ity ākāravad ayam ity ākāro 'pi kalpita eva / ubhayākārabādhe 'py adhiṣṭhānabhūtacaitanyābādhān na śūnyavādaprasaṅgaḥ / jāgraddaśāyām api śuktīdaṅkāravilakṣaṇasya prātītikasyaiva rajatedaṅkārasya bhānābhyupagamāc ca / "adhyastam eva hi parisphurati bhrameṣu" (SŚ I.36.) iti nyāyāt / śuktīidamaṃśabhānapakṣe 'pi na idamaṃśasatyatvam adhyāse prayojakam, kintv adhiṣṭhānasatyatvam / adhiṣṭhānaṃ ca tatrājñātaśukticaitanyam ivātrāpi sākṣicaitanyaṃ vidyata evety upapāditam / tasmān na pakṣadvaye 'pi kāpy anupapattiḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s>-consciousness delimited by the mind is itself the substratum — even in this view, since the concealing nature of state-specific ignorance is accepted, there is no difficulty whatsoever. For this very reason, in the various treatises (<s>śāstras</s>), such designations are found here and there. Objection: If mind-delimited consciousness is the substratum, then the cognition of an elephant [in dream] should take the form 'I am an elephant,' with the ego-sense as co-referential — just as the cognition of silver in shell takes the form 'this is silver' with the shell as co-referential — and not 'this is an elephant.' Even in the view that <s>Brahman</s>-consciousness is the substratum, the cognition should be merely of the form 'elephant' and not 'this is an elephant,' since in that case too there is equally no external object as the referent of the demonstrative 'this.' Reply: No. In the first view, since the ego-sense, like the shell, does not delimit the substratum, there is no danger of the error taking the form 'I am an elephant,' just as [in shell-silver error there is no form] 'the shell is silver.' Because the cognition 'I' — like the cognition 'this is a shell' — is opposed to error; and because the 'this'-aspect is accepted as appearing [in error] precisely as non-opposed to error. In the last view, the 'this'-form, like the 'elephant'-form, is itself superimposed. Even when both forms are sublated, since the consciousness that is the substratum is not sublated, there is no danger of the void doctrine (<s>śūnyavāda</s>). And because even in the waking state, it is accepted that what appears in the 'this'-aspect of shell-silver is the illusory (<s>prātītika</s>) 'this' of silver, distinct from the 'this' [referring to] the shell — by the principle 'only what is superimposed appears in error' (SŚ I.36). And even in the view that accepts the appearance of the 'this'-aspect of the shell, it is not the reality of the 'this'-aspect that is the cause of error, but rather the reality of the substratum. And the substratum there is the witness-consciousness (<s>sākṣicaitanya</s>), which exists [even] as the unknown shell-consciousness — this has been demonstrated here as well. Therefore, in both views there is no difficulty whatsoever.

body.text: atra ca svāpnikapadārthabhoktā taijasa ity ucyate / pittākhyatejaḥpradhānatvād ādityādijyotirantareṇāpi bhāsakatvād iti vā /
body.translated_text: And here, the experiencer of dream-objects is called <s>Taijasa</s> — either because of the predominance of the fire-element called bile (<s>pitta</s>), or because of its capacity to illuminate even without external lights such as the sun.

body.text: evaṃ jāgratsvapnabhogadvayena śrāntasya jīvasya tadubhayakāraṇakarmakṣaye jñānaśaktyavacchinnasya savāsanasyāntaḥkaraṇasya kāraṇātmanāvasthāne sati viśrāmasthānaṃ suṣuptyavasthā / na kiñcid avediṣam iti kāraṇamātropalambhaḥ suṣuptiḥ / tatra jāgratsvapnabhogyapadārthajñānābhāve 'pi sākṣyākāraṃ, sukhākāraṃ, avasthājñānākāraṃ cāvidyāyāḥ vṛttitrayam abhyupeyate / ahaṅkārābhāvāc ca naikā viśiṣṭavṛttiḥ suṣuptyabhāvaprasaṅgāt / ata eva vṛttirūpasyopalambhasyābhāvān na pralaye 'tivyāptiḥ, tatra tatkalpanābījābhāvāt, iha ca sukham aham asvāpsaṃ na kiñcid avediṣam iti suptotthitasya parāmarśāt, ananubhave ca parāmarśānupapatteḥ / antaḥkaraṇoparāgakālīnānubhavajanyatvābhāvāc ca na tattollekhābhāve 'pi smaraṇatvānupapattiḥ / smaraṇe tattollekhaniyamābhāvāc ca jāgraddaśāyām asvāpsam ity anubhavānupapatteḥ liṅgābhāvena ca āśrayāsiddhyā cānumānasyāsaṃbhavāt / ahaṅkāras tu utthānasamaya evānubhūyate / suṣuptau līnatvena tasyānanūbhūtatvāt smaraṇānupapatteḥ / mukhapratibimbāśraye darpaṇe japākusumalauhityādhyāse raktaṃ mukham iti pratītivad ahaṅkārāśrayasākṣicaitanyasya smaraṇāśrayatvāt aham asvāpsam iti sāmānādhikaraṇyapratītiḥ, na punar ahaṃ sukhīti vāśrayatayā / smṛtisaṃśayaviparyayāṇāṃ sākṣicaitanyāśrayatvaniyamād ahaṅkārasya ca pramāṇajanyajñānāśrayatvāt pramātvenaiva tatkāryatāvacchedāt, apramātvāvacchedena ca avidyāyā eva kāraṇatvāt / ata eva anāptavākyādijanyaparokṣavibhramo 'pi avidyāvṛttir evety abhyupagamo vedāntavidām / tatrāntaḥkaraṇavṛttijanakasāmagrīsambhave 'pi pramātvābhāvāvarodhenāntaḥkaraṇasyāsāmarthyāt / nāmādiṣu brahmādhyāsas tu icchādhīnatayā bhramapramāvilakṣaṇā manovṛttir eva kāmādivat / tad uktaṃ "ata eva codanājanyatvān mānasī kriyaiva sā, na jñānam" iti / etena tarkasyāpi manovṛttitvaṃ vyākhyātam / vyāpyāropeṇa vyāpakaprasañjanātmakasya tasya icchādhīnatayā bhramapramāvilakṣaṇatvāt / ata eva manananididhyāsanasahite śravaṇākhye vedāntavicāre śrotavyo mantavyo nididhyāsitavya ityādividhir upapadyate, tasya caturvidhānvayavyatirekāditarkarūpatvāt / dṛgdṛśyānvayavyatirekaḥ, sākṣisākṣyānvayavyatirekaḥ, āgamāpāyitadavadhyanvayavyatirekaḥ, duḥkhiparamapremāspadānvayavyatireka iti / anuvṛttavyāvṛttānvayavyatirekaḥ pañcamaḥ / etac ca sarveṣāṃ vedāntānukūlatarkāṇāṃ caturlakṣaṇīmīmāṃsāpratipāditānām upalakṣaṇam ity abhiyuktāḥ / vistaras tu vedāntakalpalatikāyām anusandheyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus, when the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), exhausted by the twofold experience of waking and dream, and upon the exhaustion of the <s>karma</s> (actions) that caused both states — the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), together with its impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), delimited by the power of knowledge (<s>jñānaśakti</s>), abides in its causal form — deep sleep (<s>suṣupti</s>) is the state of rest. 'I did not know anything' — deep sleep is the apprehension of the mere cause. There, even in the absence of knowledge of objects enjoyed in waking and dream, three modifications (<s>vṛtti</s>) of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) are accepted: one in the form of the witness (<s>sākṣin</s>), one in the form of bliss (<s>sukha</s>), and one in the form of state-ignorance (<s>avasthājñāna</s>). And due to the absence of the ego (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>), it is not a single qualified modification — otherwise deep sleep would be negated. Therefore, since there is no apprehension in the form of a mental modification, there is no over-extension to cosmic dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>), since there is no seed for such a postulation in that [state]; whereas here, from the recollection of the person who has awoken — 'I slept happily, I did not know anything' — and since recollection is impossible without prior experience. And since it is not produced by an experience during the time when the inner organ is engaged, there is no difficulty about memory even without such a trace. And since in the waking state the experience 'I slept' cannot occur through recollection — due to the absence of a sign [of such experience] and the failure of inference due to the unestablished substratum. The ego (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>) is experienced only at the time of awakening; since it was dissolved during deep sleep, it was not experienced then, hence its recollection would be impossible. Just as when redness from a <s>japā</s> (hibiscus) flower is superimposed on a mirror that serves as the support for a face-reflection, one has the cognition 'the face is red' — so the witness-consciousness (<s>sākṣi-caitanya</s>), which is the support of the ego, being the support of memory, gives rise to the co-referential cognition 'I slept,' not as the ego itself being the support of 'I was happy.' Because memory, doubt, and error are invariably supported by witness-consciousness, and the ego is the support of knowledge produced by valid means of knowledge — its effect being delimited by validity alone — while <s>avidyā</s> alone is the cause as delimited by invalidity. Therefore, even indirect error produced by unreliable statements and such is accepted by the <s>Vedānta</s> scholars as a modification of <s>avidyā</s> alone — because even when the conditions for producing a mental modification are present, the inner organ is incapable due to the obstruction of the absence of validity. The superimposition of <s>Brahman</s> on names and such, however, being dependent on will, is a mental modification distinct from both error and valid knowledge, like desire and so forth. As it is said: 'Therefore, being produced by injunction, it is merely a mental activity, not knowledge.' By this, reasoning (<s>tarka</s>) too is explained as a mental modification — since, being of the nature of proving the pervader through the superimposition of the pervaded, it is dependent on will and hence distinct from error and valid knowledge. Therefore, reflection (<s>manana</s>) and profound meditation (<s>nididhyāsana</s>)...
