body.text: tad evaṃ suṣuptyavasthāyām asty ānandabhogas tadbhoktā ca suṣuptyabhimānī prājña ity ucyate / prakarṣeṇājñatvāt tadānīṃ viśeṣāvacchedābhāvena prakṛṣṭajñatvād vā / tadānīṃ cāntaḥkaraṇasya laye 'pi tatsaṃskāreṇāvacchedān na jīvābhāvaprasaṅgaḥ, na vā sārvajñāpattiḥ / īśvarābhedapratipādanaṃ ca śarrirendriyādyabhimānarahitatvenopacārāt / saṃskārasya ca nimittakāraṇatvena sākṣyāśritakāryopādānakoṭāv apraveśān na tadbhede 'pi sākṣibhedaḥ / jāgaraṇe tv antaḥkaraṇasya pramāśritakāryopādānakoṭau praveśāt tadbhedena pramātṛbheda eva / sākṣiṇa eva cādhikopādhiviśiṣṭasya pramātṛtvān na pratisandhānānupapattir iti /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the state of deep sleep there is the enjoyment of bliss, and the enjoyer of that is called <s>prājña</s> — the presiding [consciousness] of deep sleep. [He is called <s>prājña</s>] either because of being intensely ignorant (<s>prakarṣeṇa ajña</s>) at that time due to the absence of particular distinctions, or because of being intensely wise (<s>prakṛṣṭa-jña</s>). And even when the inner organ has dissolved at that time, there is no unwanted consequence of the non-existence of the <s>jīva</s>, since it is delimited by the impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of that [inner organ]; nor is there the unwanted consequence of omniscience. And the teaching of non-difference from <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) is [established by the <s>Śruti</s>] regarding the embodied...

children.text: mātṛmānaprabhede 'pi pratidehaṃ na bhidyate /
children.translated_text: Even when the knower, the means of knowledge, and so forth differ, [the witness] does not differ from body to body.

children.text: sākṣī bāhyārthavad yasmāt sa ātmety ucyate tataḥ //
children.translated_text: Since the witness (<s>sākṣin</s>) is like an external object [in being self-evident], it is therefore called the <s>ātman</s> (Self).

children.text: vyabhicāro mitho yadvat pramātrādeḥ svasākṣikaḥ /
children.translated_text: Although the knower and so forth mutually vary, being objects of their own witness,

children.text: sarvamātrādyabhāvārthasākṣitvān na tathātmanaḥ // (BAUBhV III.4.54-55.)
children.translated_text: the <s>ātman</s> is not like that, since it is the witness of the absence of all knowers and so forth. (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad Bhāṣyavārtika</s> III.4.54-55)

body.text: iti vārtikakārapādair vyavahāradaśāyām api sākṣibhedanirākaraṇāt suṣuptau tadbhedakalpanaṃ keṣāñcid vyāmohamātram ity avadheyam /
body.translated_text: Thus, since the <s>Vārtikakāra</s> (<s>Sureśvara</s>) has refuted the difference of the witness even in the state of empirical dealings (<s>vyavahāra</s>), the postulation of its difference in deep sleep by some is to be noted as mere delusion.

body.text: nanu, duḥkham aham asvāpsam iti kasyacit kadācit parāmarśāt suṣuptau duḥkhānubhavo 'py astu / na, tadānīṃ duḥkhasāmagrīviraheṇa tadabhāvāt / sukhasya cātmasvarūpatvena nityatvāt śayyāder asamīcīnatve ca duḥkham ity upacārāt duḥkham aham asvāpsam iti pratyayopapattiḥ / atha vā avasthātrayasyāpi traividhyāṅgīkārāt suṣuptāv api duḥkham upapadyate / tathā hi pramājñānaṃ jāgrajjāgrat, śuktirajatādivibhramo jāgratsvapnaḥ, śramādinā stabdhībhāvo jāgratsuṣuptiḥ / evaṃ svapne mantrādiprāptiḥ svapnajāgrat, svapne 'pi svapno mayā dṛṣṭa iti buddhiḥ svapnasvapnaḥ, jāgraddaśāyāṃ kathayituṃ na śakyate svapnāvasthāyāṃ ca yatkiñcid anubhūyate tatsvapnasuṣuptiḥ / evaṃ suṣuptyavasthāyām api sātvikī yā sukhākārā vṛttiḥ sā suṣuptijāgrat, tadanantaraṃ sukham aham asvāpsam iti parāmarśaḥ, tatraiva yā rājasī vṛttiḥ sā suṣuptisvapnaḥ, tadanantaram eva duḥkham aham asvāpsam iti parāmarśopapattiḥ, tatraiva yā tāmasī vṛttiḥ sā suṣuptisuṣuptiḥ, tadanantaraṃ gāḍhaṃ mūḍho 'ham āsam iti parāmarśaḥ / yathā caitat tathā vāsiṣṭhavārtikāmṛtādau spaṣṭam /
body.translated_text: Objection: Since someone sometimes recollects 'I slept unhappily,' there should be an experience of suffering in deep sleep too. No — because at that time, due to the absence of the conditions for suffering, suffering does not exist. And since bliss is eternal, being the very nature of the Self (<s>ātmasvarūpa</s>), when the bed and so forth are not proper, 'suffering' is used figuratively. Thus the cognition 'I slept unhappily' is explained. Alternatively, even the three states...

body.text: evam adhyātmaṃ viśvaḥ, adhibhūtaṃ virāṭ, adhidaivaṃ viṣṇuḥ, adhyātmaṃ jāgrat, adhidaivaṃ pālanaṃ, adhibhūtaṃ sattvaguṇaḥ / evam adhyātmaṃ taijasaḥ, adhibhūtaṃ hiraṇyagarbhaḥ, adhidaivaṃ brahmāḥ, adhyātmaṃ svapnaḥ, adhidaivaṃ sṛṣṭiḥ, adhibhūtaṃ rajoguṇaḥ / evaṃ adhyātmaṃ prājñaḥ, adhibhūtam avyākṛtaṃ, adhidaivaṃ rudraḥ, adhyātmaṃ suṣuptiḥ, adhidaivaṃ pralayaḥ, adhibhūtaṃ tamoguṇaḥ / evam adhyātmādhibhūtādhidevānām ekatvāt praṇavāvayavatrayasahitānām eteṣām upahitānām aikyopāsanayā hiraṇyagarbhalokaprāptiḥ, antaḥkaraṇaśuddhidvārā kramamuktiś ca / etat sarvopādhinirākāraṇena sākṣicaitanyamātrajñānena tu sākṣād eva mokṣa iti / tad evaṃ trayāṇām apy avasthātrayasahitānāṃ viśvataijasaprājñānām avidyātmakatvāt dṛ.śyatvena ca mithyātvād anupahitaḥ kevalaḥ sākṣī turīyākhyo 'ham asmīty arthaḥ / evaṃ vyavahārataḥ sarvavyavasthopapatteḥ paramārthataḥ kasyā apy avasthāyā abhāvān na kāpy anupapattiḥ / vistareṇa caitat prapañcitam asmābhir vedāntakalpalatikāyām ity uparamyate // 8 //
body.translated_text: Thus: in the <s>adhyātma</s> (individual) aspect, [the waker is] <s>Viśva</s>; in the <s>adhibhūta</s> (cosmic) aspect, <s>Virāṭ</s>; in the <s>adhidaiva</s> (divine) aspect, <s>Viṣṇu</s>. In the <s>adhyātma</s> aspect, waking; in the <s>adhidaiva</s> aspect, preservation; in the <s>adhibhūta</s> aspect, <s>sattva-guṇa</s> (quality of goodness). Similarly: in the <s>adhyātma</s> aspect, <s>Taijasa</s> (the dreamer); in the <s>adhibhūta</s> aspect, <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>; in the <s>adhidaiva</s> aspect, <s>Brahmā</s>. In the <s>adhyātma</s> aspect, dream; in the <s>adhidaiva</s> aspect, creation; in the <s>adhibhūta</s> aspect, <s>rajo-guṇa</s> (quality of passion). Similarly: in the <s>adhyātma</s> aspect, <s>Prājña</s> (the deep sleeper); in the <s>adhibhūta</s> aspect, the Unmanifest (<s>avyākṛta</s>)...

body.text: nanu, jāgratsvapnasuṣuptyavasthāsahitānāṃ trayāṇām api tadabhimānināṃ mithyātvāt, tatsākṣiṇo 'pi mithyātvaṃ syāt, aviśaṣāt, ity āśaṅkya viśeṣābhidhānena sākṣiṇaḥ satyatvam āha --
body.translated_text: Objection: Since all three [states] — the presiding entities of waking, dream, and deep sleep — are false, the witness of those would also be false, due to the absence of distinction. Anticipating this objection, he states the reality of the witness by specifying its distinction:

children.text: api vyāpakatvād dhitatvaprayogāt svataḥ siddhabhāvād ananyāśrayatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because of its all-pervasiveness, because the word 'that' (<s>tat</s>) is used [to refer to it], because its existence is self-established, and because it has no other support —

children.text: jagattuccham etat samastaṃ tad anyat tad eko 'vaśiṣṭaḥ śivaḥ kevalo 'ham // 9 //
children.translated_text: this entire world is insubstantial, all that is other [than the Self is unreal]; that One alone remains — I am <s>Śiva</s>, the Absolute. || 9 ||

body.text: "na dṛṣṭer draṣṭāraṃ paśyeḥ" (BAU III.4.2.) iti sākṣiṇaṃ prakṛtya "ato 'nyad ārtam" (BAU III.4.2.) iti śruteḥ sākṣiṇo 'nyat sākṣyaṃ sarvaṃ jagattucchaṃ, na tu sākṣī / bādhāvadhitvāt bhramādhiṣṭhānatayā jñātatvāc ca, tadbādhagrāhakābhāvāc cetyādyanuktasamuccayārthaḥ apiśabdaḥ / "atha yad alpaṃ tat martyam" (ChU VII.24.1.) iti śruteḥ paricchinnatvatucchatvayoḥ samavyāptatvāt paricchinnatvanivṛttyā tucchatvanivṛttir ity āha -- vyāpakatvād iti / "sarvaṃ khalv idaṃ brahma" (ChU III.14.1.) iti sarvātmatvopadeśena deśakālāparicchinnatvāt, ākāśādīnāṃ ca deśakālaparichinnatve 'py āpekṣikamahattvena vyāpakatvopacārāt / nanu, sarvavyāpakatvena nityatvād bhāvarūpatvāc cātmā na duḥkhanivṛttirūpaḥ, nāpi sukharūpaḥ, sukhasyānityatvena nityātmarūpatvānupapatteḥ, tathā cātmasvarūpo mokṣo 'puruṣārtha evety āśaṅkya, na, ityāha -- hitatvaprayogād iti / hitatvaṃ, puruṣārthatvam / "tad etat preyaḥ putrāt preyo vittāt preyo 'nyasmāt sarvasmād antarataraṃ yad ayam ātmeti" (BAU I.4.8.) "yo vai bhūmā tat sukhaṃ" (ChU VII.23.1.) "eṣa eva parama ānandaḥ" (BAU IV.3.33.) "vijñānam ānandaṃ brahma" (BAU III.9.28.) ityādiśrutibhyas tasya paramānandarūpatvopadeśāt / tasya ca nityatve 'pi loke dharmajanyatattadantaḥkaraṇavṛttivyaṅgyatayā tadutpattivināśopacāraḥ / ajñānavyavahitasya ca tasyāprāptasyeva jñānamātrād avidyānivṛttyā prāptir iva bhavatīti taduddeśena mumukṣupravṛttyupapattiḥ / adhyastasya prapañcasya duḥkhasvarūpasyādhiṣṭhānatvāt sa evābhāva iti duḥkhābhāvarūpatvenāpi tasya puruṣārthatā /
body.translated_text: From the <s>śruti</s> 'You cannot see the seer of sight' (BĀU III.4.2), taking the witness (<s>sākṣin</s>) as the subject, the <s>śruti</s> 'Anything other than this is afflicted' (BĀU III.4.2) [teaches that] everything other than the witness — the entire witnessed universe — is insubstantial (<s>tuccha</s>), but not the witness. The word 'also' (<s>api</s>) serves to include additional [reasons] not stated: because [the world] has a limit of sublation, because it is known as the substratum of error, and because there is no [subsequent] cognition that would sublate it. From the <s>śruti</s> 'Now, that which is finite is mortal' (ChU VII.24.1), since limitedness and insubstantiality are co-extensive, by the removal of limitedness there is removal of insubstantiality — hence he says: 'because of being all-pervading.' From the teaching of being the self of all in 'All this indeed is <s>Brahman</s>' (ChU III.14.1), it is unlimited by space and time; and even though space etc. are limited by space and time, they are figuratively called 'pervading' due to their relative greatness. Objection: Since the <s>ātman</s>, being all-pervading and therefore eternal and of the nature of a positive entity, is not of the nature of the cessation of suffering, nor of the nature of pleasure — because pleasure, being non-eternal, cannot be the nature of the eternal <s>ātman</s> — therefore <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), being the nature of the self, would not be a <s>puruṣārtha</s> (goal of life). Anticipating this, he says: 'because of the use of the word beneficial (<s>hitatva</s>).' <s>Hitatva</s> means being a <s>puruṣārtha</s>. From <s>śrutis</s> such as 'This self is dearer than a son, dearer than wealth, dearer than everything else, being the innermost' (BĀU I.4.8); 'That which is the Infinite (<s>Bhūman</s>) is happiness' (ChU VII.23.1); 'This indeed is the supreme bliss' (BĀU IV.3.33); 'Consciousness and bliss is <s>Brahman</s>' (BĀU III.9.28) — since the teaching is that its nature is supreme bliss. And though it is eternal, in the world the figurative usage of its arising and ceasing occurs because it is manifested through the respective mental modifications of the inner organ produced by <s>dharma</s> (merit). And for that [bliss] which is as if unattained due to being concealed by <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance), through mere knowledge, by the removal of <s>avidyā</s>, there is as it were an attainment — thus the effort of the aspirant for liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>) toward that goal is explained. And since the <s>ātman</s> is the substratum of the superimposed phenomenal world whose nature is suffering, its very non-existence constitutes the absence of suffering — thus even as the absence of suffering, it serves as a <s>puruṣārtha</s>.

body.text: nanu, mokṣe sukhaṃ saṃvedyate na vā / nādyaḥ, tadānīṃ dehendriyādyabhāvena tadvyañjakābhāvāt, vyañjakābhāve 'pi tatsaṃvedanābhyupagame saṃsāradaśāyām api tathā prasaṅgāt / na dvitīyaḥ, apuruṣārthatvāpatteḥ, jñāyamānasyaiva tasya puruṣārthatvāt / ata eva śarkarātadbhojinor iveti vaiṣṇavaṃ manyamānānām udgāra iti cet, na, ityāha -- svataḥ siddhabhāvād iti / svaprakāśajñānarūpatvād ity arthaḥ / yady api saṃsāradaśāyām avidyāvṛtarūpatvād ātmā paramānandarūpatayā na prathate tathāpi tattvavidyayāvidyānivṛttau svaprakāśatayā svayam eva paramānandarūpeṇa prakāśata iti na vyañjakāpekṣā / nanu, sukhasya svaprakāśajñānarūpatve 'pi nātmarūpatā, jñānasya dhātvartharūpatayā kriyātvena sāśrayatvāt jānāmīti pratīteḥ, jñānam aham asmīty apratīteś ca / tathā ca katham advaitavāda ity āśaṅkya, na, ity āha -- ananyāśrayatvād iti / "yatsākṣād aparokṣād brahma ya ātmā sārvāntaraḥ" (BAU III.4.1.) ityādiśruteḥ svaprakāśajñānānandarūpa evātmā, antaḥkaraṇatādātmyādhyāsena ca tadvṛttau jñānādhyāsāj jānāmīti tadāśrayatvapratītiḥ / dhātvarthatvam utpattivināśavattvaṃ cāntaḥkaraṇavṛtter iti jñaptirūpamukhajñānasya sarvādhiṣṭhānatvenānyāśrayatvābhāvān na dvaitāpattiḥ / tena jñānasukhātmaka ātmā satyas tadbhinnaṃ ca sarvaṃ jagad asatyam iti siddham // 9 //
body.translated_text: Objection: In liberation, is bliss experienced or not? Not the first, because at that time, due to the absence of body, senses, etc., there is no manifesting agent; and if experience is accepted even without a manifesting agent, the same would follow even in the state of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Not the second, because then it would not be a <s>puruṣārtha</s>, since only what is known is a goal of life. Therefore, just as sweetness and the one who tastes it [are distinct], this is merely a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>-like 'belch' [of dualistic devotionalism]. Answer: No — he says: 'Because of being self-established in nature.' The meaning is: because of being of the nature of self-luminous consciousness. Though in the state of <s>saṃsāra</s> the <s>ātman</s> does not manifest as supreme bliss because its nature is concealed by <s>avidyā</s>, nevertheless, when <s>avidyā</s> is removed by the knowledge of reality, it manifests by itself as supreme bliss through self-luminosity — thus there is no dependence on a manifesting agent. Objection: Even if bliss is of the nature of self-luminous consciousness, it is not the nature of the <s>ātman</s>, because knowledge, being of the nature of a verbal root-meaning, is an activity and therefore has a locus, as evidenced by the cognition 'I know'; and because there is no cognition 'I am knowledge.' And thus, how can the Advaita doctrine [hold]? Answer: No — he says: 'Because it has no other locus.' From the <s>śruti</s>: 'That which is directly, immediately <s>Brahman</s>, which is the self, the innermost of all' (BĀU III.4.1) — the <s>ātman</s> is indeed of the nature of self-luminous consciousness and bliss. The cognition 'I know' and the perception of it having a locus arise through the superimposition of the identity of the inner organ upon [the self], and thereby the superimposition of knowledge upon the mental modification. The nature of a verbal root-meaning and the possession of arising and ceasing belong to the mental modification. Since the primary consciousness, which is of the nature of awareness, is the substratum of all and therefore has no other locus — there is no fall into duality. Therefore it is established that the <s>ātman</s>, whose nature is consciousness and bliss, is real, and that the entire universe different from it is unreal. // 9 //

body.text: nanu, sarvasya jagatas tucchatve tanniṣedhenātmatattvapratipattir na syāt / na hi śaśaviṣāṇaṃ niṣidhyate, kvacit pramitaṃ kvacin niṣidhyata iti nyāyāt / tathā ca niṣedhānupapattyaiva na jagatas tucchatvam iti, na, ity āha --
body.translated_text: Objection: If the entire universe is insubstantial, then the apprehension of the truth of the <s>ātman</s> through its negation would not be possible. For a hare's horn is not negated, [following] the principle that what has been cognized somewhere is negated elsewhere. And thus, by the very impossibility of negation, the universe is not insubstantial. Answer: No — he says:

children.text: na caikaṃ tadanyad dvitīyaṃ kutaḥ syāt na vā kevalatvaṃ na cākevalatvam /
children.translated_text: There is not one, nor a second other [than That] — whence could it be? Neither mere oneness, nor non-oneness.

children.text: na śūnyaṃ na cāśūnyam advaitakatvāt kathaṃ sarvavedāntasiddhaṃ bravīmi // 10 //
children.translated_text: Neither void, nor non-void — because of being non-dual. How shall I express that which is established by all <s>Vedānta</s>? // 10 //

body.text: ekatvasaṅkhyāyogi ekam / tad apekṣābuddhijanyadvitvasaṅkhyāyogi dvitīyam / tata ekābhāve dvitīyaṃ kutaḥ syāt / dvitīyaṃ ca tṛtīyādīnām apy upalakṣaṇam / nanu, "ekam evādvitīyam" (ChU VI.2.1.) iti śrutyā ekatvaṃ pratipādyate / na, ity āha -- na vā kevalatvam iti / kevalam ekatvaṃ, tasyāvidyakatvāt / yady ātmana ekatvaṃ śrutyā na pratipādyate, tarhi pratyakṣādipramāṇavaśād anekatvaṃ syād iti cet, na, ity āha -- na cākevalatvam iti / akevalatvam anekatvaṃ, "neha nānāsti kiñcana" (BAU IV.4.19.), "ekam evādvitīyam" (ChU VI.2.1.), "athāta ādeśo neti neti" (BAU II.3.6.) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ / tarhi sarvapratiṣedhāc chūnyam eva syād iti, na, ity āha -- na śūnyam iti, "asann eva sa bhavati asad brahmeti veda cet, asti brahmeti ced veda santam enaṃ tato vidur iti" (TU II.6.), "satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ brahma" (TU II.1.) "sad eva somyedam agra āsīt" (ChU VI.2.1.) ity upakramya "aitadātmyam idaṃ sarvaṃ tat satyaṃ sa ātmā tat tvam asi" (ChU VI.8.7.) ityādiśrutibhiḥ satyatvajñānatvādidharmavad api syāt, na, ity āha -- na cāśūnyam iti / ekam advitīyam iti padadvayena sarvabhedapratiṣedhe 'py evakāreṇa dharmadharmibhāvādibhedābhedapratiṣedhāt / sarvatra hetum āha -- advaitakatvād iti / dvidhā itaṃ dvītaṃ tasya bhāvo dvaitam / tad uktaṃ vārtike "dvidhetaṃ dvītam ity āhus tadbhāvo dvaitam ucyate" (BAUBhV IV.3.1807.) iti / na vidyate dvaitaṃ dvidhābhāvo yatra tad advaitam ity akṣarārthaḥ / "salila eko dṛṣṭādvaitaḥ" (BAU IV.3.32.) itiśruteḥ / pratiyogijñānasyaiva lāghavenābhāvabuddhau kāraṇatvāt dvaitasyānirvacanīyatvāṅgīkāreṇa pratyakṣādivedyatvān niṣedhopapattir ity arthaḥ / tarhy etādṛśa ātmā aṅulinirdeśena pratipādyatām iti, na, ity āha -- kathaṃ bravīmīti / kim ākṣepe? advaitakatvena vāgaviṣayatvāt, "avacanenaiva provāca" (NUU VII.), "yato vāco nivartante aprāpya mānasā saha" (TU II.4.), "na vijñāner vijñātāraṃ vijānīyāḥ" (BAU III.4.2.) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ / vāgaviṣayatve kathaṃ vedāntānāṃ tatra prāmāṇyam iti cet, na, aviṣaye 'py ātmani tadākāravṛttimātreṇa tadavidyānivartakatvād ity āha -- sarvavedāntasiddham iti / tathā ca śrutiḥ "yasyāmataṃ tasya mataṃ mataṃ yasya na veda saḥ / avijñātaṃ vijānatāṃ vijñātam avijānatām" (KU II.3.), "yan manasā na manute yenāhur mano mataṃ, tad eva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yad idam upāsate" (KU I.5.) ityādir aviṣayatvam ātmano darśayati / tad evaṃ vedāntavākyajanyākhaṇdākāravṛttyā avidyānivṛttau tatkalpitasakalānarthanivṛttau paramānandarūpaḥ san kṛtakṛtyo bhavatīti siddham // 10 //
body.translated_text: That which is associated with the number 'one' is 'one.' That which is associated with the number 'two,' dependent on [the concept of] 'one,' is 'second.' Therefore, in the absence of one, whence a second? And 'second' is a representative term (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) for third, etc. as well. Objection: But oneness is taught by the <s>śruti</s>: 'One only, without a second' (ChU VI.2.1). Answer: No — he says: 'Nor mere oneness.' Mere oneness — because that [oneness] belongs to <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). If oneness is not taught by <s>śruti</s>, then through the force of perceptual and other means of knowledge, there would be non-oneness (multiplicity). Answer: No — he says: 'Nor non-oneness.' Non-oneness means multiplicity — [refuted] by <s>śrutis</s> such as 'There is no diversity here whatsoever' (BĀU IV.4.19), 'One only, without a second' (ChU VI.2.1), 'Now the teaching: not this, not this' (BĀU II.3.6). Then, from the negation of everything, it would be mere void? Answer: No — he says: 'Not void' — [citing] 'He who knows <s>Brahman</s> as non-existent becomes himself non-existent; he who knows <s>Brahman</s> as existing, him they know as existing' (TU II.6); '<s>Brahman</s> is truth, knowledge, infinite' (TU II.1); beginning with 'Being alone, dear one, this was in the beginning' (ChU VI.2.1) and concluding with 'All this has That as its self; That is the truth; He is the self; that thou art' (ChU VI.8.7). Nor would it be endowed with attributes like truth, consciousness, etc.? Answer: No — he says: 'Nor non-void.' Because by the two words 'one' and 'without a second,' even though all difference is negated, by the emphatic particle 'eva' (indeed), difference of attribute and attribute-possessor, etc., is also negated. He states the reason for all this: 'Because of being non-dual (<s>advaitakatva</s>).' 'Divided in two (<s>dvidhā</s>) is <s>dvīta</s>; its state is <s>dvaita</s> (duality).' As stated in the <s>Vārttika</s>: 'They say that what is divided in two is <s>dvīta</s>; its state is called <s>dvaita</s>' (BAUBhV IV.3.1807). That in which there is no <s>dvaita</s> (duality), no state of division — that is <s>advaita</s> (non-duality): this is the literal meaning of the word. From the <s>śruti</s>: 'In water, a single seer, non-dual' (BĀU IV.3.32). Since the knowledge of the counter-positive alone is the cause of the cognition of absence, and since duality is acknowledged as indescribable (<s>anirvacanīya</s>), negation is possible because it is knowable by perception, etc. — this is the meaning. Then let such an <s>ātman</s> be pointed out by a finger? Answer: No — he says: 'How shall I express (<s>kathaṃ bravīmi</s>)?' Is this a question? No, [it is an expression of impossibility:] because, being non-dual, it is beyond the reach of speech — from <s>śrutis</s> such as 'He taught by not speaking at all' (NUU VII); 'From which words return, together with the mind, without reaching it' (TU II.4); 'You cannot know the knower of knowledge' (BĀU III.4.2). If it is beyond the reach of speech, how can the <s>Vedānta</s> texts be authoritative regarding it? Answer: Because even regarding the <s>ātman</s> that is beyond [speech], merely by assuming its form in a mental modification, they serve to remove the <s>avidyā</s> regarding it — he says: 'Established by all <s>Vedānta</s>.' And the <s>śruti</s> [says]: 'He by whom it is not conceived, by him it is conceived; he by whom it is conceived does not know it. Unknown to those who know, known to those who do not know' (KU II.3); 'That which the mind does not think, by which, they say, the mind is thought — know that alone as <s>Brahman</s>, not this which people worship here' (KU I.5) — and such [passages] show the <s>ātman</s> to be beyond objectification. Thus, when <s>avidyā</s> is removed by the indivisible-form mental modification (<s>akhaṇḍākāravṛtti</s>) born of <s>Vedānta</s> sentences, and when all the miseries imagined by <s>avidyā</s> are thereby removed, [the aspirant], being of the nature of supreme bliss, becomes one whose purpose is fulfilled. This is established. // 10 //

children.text: na staumi taṃ vyāsam aśeṣam arthaṃ samyaṅ na sūtrair api yo babandha /
children.translated_text: I do not praise <s>Vyāsa</s>, who did not completely bind the entire meaning even through the <s>Sūtras</s>.

children.text: vināpi taiḥ saṅgrathitākhilārthaṃ taṃ śaṅkaraṃ staumi sureśvaraṃ ca // 1 //
children.translated_text: I praise <s>Śaṅkara</s> and <s>Sureśvara</s>, who gathered the complete meaning even without those [Sūtras]. // 1 //

children.text: laghur api bahvarthavahaś cintāmaṇir iva nibandho 'yam /
children.translated_text: This treatise, though brief, carries abundant meaning, like a wish-fulfilling gem (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>),

children.text: madhusūdanena muninā vihito guṇināṃ vinodāya // 2 //
children.translated_text: composed by the sage <s>Madhusūdana</s> for the delight of the discerning. // 2 //

children.text: yad atra sauṣṭhavaṃ kiñcit tadguror iva me na hi /
children.translated_text: Whatever excellence there is here, that belongs to the <s>guru</s>, not to me.

children.text: yad atrāsauṣṭhavaṃ kiñcit tan mamaiva guror na hi // 3 //
children.translated_text: Whatever deficiency there is here, that is mine alone, not the <s>guru</s>'s. // 3 //

children.text: bahuyācanayā mayāyamalpo balabhadrasya kṛe kṛto nibandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Through much entreaty, this brief treatise has been composed by me for the sake of <s>Balabhadra</s>.

children.text: yad aduṣṭam ihāsti yac ca duṣṭaṃ tadudārāḥ sudhiyo vivecayantu // 4 //
children.translated_text: Whatever is faultless here, and whatever is faulty — let the noble wise ones discriminate that. || 4 ||

body.text: iti śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakācāryaśrīviśveśvarasarasvatībhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyaśrīmadhusūdanasarasvatīviracitaḥ siddhāntabindunāmā granthaḥ samāptaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus is completed the work named <s>Siddhāntabindu</s> (Drop of the Established Doctrine), composed by <s>Śrī Madhusūdana Sarasvatī</s>, the disciple of the revered <s>Śrī Viśveśvara Sarasvatī</s>, the supreme <s>paramahaṃsa</s> (great ascetic) and wandering monk (<s>parivrājakācārya</s>).
